meaning: Per-transition reconciliation of each retained legacy model with the active spec tree: every action (but init and step) and named scenario names the successor definitions that carry it, the reason the successor abstracts it, or the gap still open in the spec that should own it.

close.note: Closure (login confirmation) makes the member closed and private, drops every session, the X link and pending X flows, withdraws mail consent and cancels waiting mail.

connectX.note: X link is committed only from the X callback for a flow bound to a live session of an open member and the X identity stays reserved; successor splits it into startX/claimXCallback/commitX.

join.note: First sign-in admits an open public member and issues a session; closed members cannot sign in through this path (canRefuseClosedSignIn).

optIn.note: Mail consent changes only through the member's own signed-in session with compare-and-set on the preference revision and destination version.

otherSession.note: A second sign-in appends another live session for the same member.

revoke.note: Sign-out deletes the caller's session and revocation removes only a session of the caller's own account.

closureTest.note: Closure ends every session and the X reservation persists; closure never touches funded awards (obligation preservation is in spec/security/continuity.md stepClosureKeepsObligations).

currentSignoutTest.note: Signing out the current session keeps the member's other sessions.

reopenTest.note: Explicit reopening readmits a closed member as public without restoring the removed X link.

consent.note: Reporter consents to the exact currently observed reporter wallet before any intent is prepared.

prepare.note: The payer prepares the generation-0 intent only for the consented reporter wallet.

retire.note: Retirement is not a separate transition: certified retirement evidence of the prior generation is a precondition of recover and is archived with it.

settle.note: Each finalized leg (researcher or fee) is recorded once against the active intent generation and stays paid.

successor.note: A successor intent (generation+1) needs certified retirement and renewed consent and changes only unpaid legs; prior generations are retained.

walletChange.note: A changed reporter wallet holds the unpaid researcher leg; successor keeps the old consent record but authorizedWallets requires consent to equal the new wallet, which is equivalent to clearing consent.

recoveryTest.note: One leg paid under generation 0, wallet change, retirement plus renewed consent, then the remaining leg paid under the successor.

unresolvedPlanTest.note: After a wallet change the unretired intent stays active and the researcher leg is held, not retired.

ban.note: A ban arrives in a newer authority snapshot and blocks new commitments without touching committed awards.

pledge.note: A pledged program has no fresh covering vault funds, so railFor never selects VaultRail; spec/security/program.md observeFunding keeps such a program Pledged, never money.

related.note: A related reporter is identified from the authority snapshot at award decision, which makes a pending proposal that commits nothing.

reserve.note: An award reserves only with fresh covering vault funds, first qualifying root cause, no restriction or ban, and approved related-party review.

restrict.note: Program restriction arrives in the authority snapshot (programRestricted) and blocks new commitments.

review.note: An independent current moderator who is not a prior decider approves or refuses the related-party award.

capTest.note: Reserved total equals the open vault holds and a reservation needs covering free funds.

fundedAwardSurvivesBanTest.note: A committed award keeps its amount and commitment through later authority snapshots including a ban.

relatedReviewTest.note: A related-party award commits only after an approved independent review.

beginVerification.note: Successor merges begin and verify into one atomic verify that compares the revision read at request start; the same-account binding is accounts.md canVerifyEmail (sender's own enrollment).

expire.note: Expiry is not an action: a request stops being pending once now reaches expiresAt (30 minutes).

optOut.note: Opt-out is a consent save that needs no destination version and advances the preference revision.

request.note: A request records the requested consent with idempotency, rate limits and cancellation of earlier pending requests.

verify.note: Verification consumes the token, records a new destination version and copies the requested consent, only if the revision read is unchanged.

admittedBeforeExpiryCanFinishTest.note: Successor verify checks pending(v, now) at the single atomic write with the live clock, so a verification begun before expiry is refused if the clock passes expiresAt before the write; legacy lets it finish. anotherActorCannotVerifyTest.note: Verification looks up the token only in the signed-in sender's own enrollment, so another account's token cannot verify.

consumedTokenCannotVerifyAgainTest.note: A consumed request is not pending, so its token cannot verify again.

expiredTokenTest.note: An expired request is not pending and cannot verify.

freshVerificationAfterOptOutTest.note: A verification after an opt-out reads the new revision and applies its requested consent as new explicit consent.

optOutWinsTest.note: An opt-out between the revision read and the verifying write refuses verification.

verificationTest.note: Verification applies the activity-only consent requested with it.

callback.note: The callback claims a live pending flow once by matching state and cookie and clears the PKCE verifier.

chooseLocal.note: A flow is started in LocalHandoff mode (PointsWeb audience only).

consume.note: An issued, unexpired, unconsumed assertion of the matching audience is consumed once.

failCallback.note: Only the GitHub exchange handler fails a processing flow.

issue.note: Production flows issue the unexpired stored assertion; local flows are delivered by pollLocal without an assertion.

storeAssertion.note: A production flow's ready poll stores one assertion with a 90 s lifetime; local flows never get assertions.

tick.note: Trusted worker clock advances time.

verify.note: The exchange completes a live processing flow with a complete GitHub identity.

expiredClaimFailsTest.note: An expired processing flow can still fail and must settle (weak fairness), never staying processing.

expiryDuringCallbackTest.note: Completion requires the flow to be live, so a flow that expires during the callback never gets an identity.

failedExchangeTest.note: A failed exchange leaves the flow CallbackFailed.

identityTest.note: Full OAuth flow ends in one consumed assertion.

localHandoffTest.note: Local handoff is delivered with no assertion.

beginCleanup.note: The hourly job deletes expired rate windows; successor merges the captured cleanup stamp and delete into one atomic purge.

capture.note: identity.md counts a rate window atomically at s.now (countRequest/admitted); it does not model the request phases of workers/identity/rate-limit.ts. Add: the request captures its stamp once, a digest-hash failure answers 503 consuming no quota, a SQL failure before the upsert answers 503 with no count, a committed count is not undone by an invalid/lost reply (a retry consumes another count), and Retry-After = window expiry minus the captured stamp.

cleanupFailure.note: A failed atomic purge commits nothing, so it is the absence of a purgeExpired step in identity.md; no state change to model.

begin.note: The source writer saves each recipient's notice in its own transaction; begin/commit are one atomic save keyed by (key, recipient).

beginOpen.note: Successor merges begin/finish into one atomic open evaluated against an authority check carrying the roster version.

commit.note: A committed save adds at most one notice per key and recipient.

finishOpen.note: A review row is shown only to a current moderator recipient while the source still allows it (penalty not reversed / case escalated, not the author or appellant).

markRead.note: Only the notice's recipient marks it read, once.

openFailure.note: An unavailable authority check returns RetryLater and never shows the item.

revokeModerator.note: The configuration release replaces the moderator roster and advances its version.

rollback.note: A failed source write commits neither the source change nor its notice; notifications.md models only the atomic committed save, so rollback is the absence of a step.

differentSourceKeepsPriorReadStateTest.note: Existing notices keep their read time when later notices are added.

failedBatchPublishesNeitherSourceNorNoti.note: Atomic save: a failed source batch commits nothing; the source change itself is owned by each writer's spec, not notifications.md.

failedReviewReadDoesNotBecomeRedirectTes.note: An unavailable check yields RetryLater, never Shown.

independentReadTest.note: Reading one recipient's notice sets only its readAt.

invalidTargetPreventsReviewRedirectTest.note: Review link targets are a presentation table (notifications.md 'titles and links stay a presentation table'); link validity is a shell concern, not a modeled state.

oneRecipientCannotReadTheOtherCopyTest.note: canRead requires the reader to be the notice recipient.

ownReviewNoticeAndSourcePermitOpenTest.note: A current moderator's own review row with a standing source is shown.

replayTest.note: Replaying the same source and recipient adds nothing and keeps the read state.

revokedRoleRefusesNewOpenTest.note: A former moderator is no longer in the roster, so the review row is not shown.

roleIsCapturedForTheCurrentOpenTest.note: Deliberately superseded: moderation.md says every open rechecks the current roster and refuses a stale check (lawStaleRosterRefused), so a revocation between check and open refuses instead of honouring the captured role.

sameSourceCanNotifyTwoRecipientsOnceTest.note: Notices are unique per (key, recipient), so two recipients get one copy each even on replay.

sourceRefusalPreventsReviewRedirectTest.note: A source that no longer allows the review (reversed penalty, unescalated case) hides the row.

sourceWithNoEligibleRecipientHasNoNotice.note: Recipient selection belongs to each source writer (e.g. moderation.md addOnce ignores recipient <= 0); save is per recipient, so an empty audience saves no notice.

authorize.note: An item is published only when the read's captured actor has current assessable access to the exact binding.

complete.note: A matching accepted final outcome at or after the gap resolves it.

exhausted.note: AttemptsExhausted settles the delivery but keeps incompleteSince.

incomplete.note: A SourceIncomplete outcome records incompleteSince once and keeps the earliest gap.

read.note: A read projects the unresolved gap for the pull request after authentication and scope checks.

retry.note: A waiting delivery is reclaimed when due; the gap survives the claim.

revoke.note: Denied or uncertain authority publishes no item.

tick.note: Time advances.

completedSourceHiddenTest.note: A completed assessment resolves the gap and the read yields no item.

gapSurvivesExhaustionTest.note: Exhausted attempts never resolve the gap and the item stays visible.

laterGapRemainsTest.note: An outcome completed before a newer gap cannot resolve it.

accepted.note: A prepared attempt's provider acceptance becomes ProviderAccepted.

acknowledge.note: Only the recipient with current case access acknowledges a case notice.

bounced.note: Independent bounce evidence moves an accepted row to Bounced.

claim.note: A due queued or retrying row is claimed with its attempt incremented within the five-attempt bound.

confirmedNotAccepted.note: Independent NotAccepted evidence for the exact attempt and digest reconciles an ambiguous row.

delivered.note: Only independent delivery evidence moves an accepted row to Delivered.

preparationFailed.note: A preparation failure retries with backoff or exhausts at the fifth attempt without a provider call.

prepare.note: Preparation rechecks authority, consent and destination and binds the destination digest before any provider call.

prepareDenied.note: Denied access or lost consent at preparation suppresses the attempt without a provider call.

rejected.note: A documented quota rejection retries or exhausts; difference: successor treats any other thrown send as Ambiguous rather than a definite retryable rejection.

retry.note: Successor merges confirmation and retry: NotAccepted evidence moves the row directly to Retrying (or Exhausted at the fifth attempt).

revoke.note: A committed consent withdrawal suppresses waiting rows; a claimed attempt is not recalled.

revokeAuthority.note: Authority is an input read at preparation from the current audience facts; loss of the role yields Denied at the next preparation.

unknown.note: A thrown send or a stale claim becomes Ambiguous and is never resent automatically.

ambiguousTest.note: An ambiguous send retries only after independent not-accepted evidence.

authorityLostBeforePreparationRefusesTes.note: Lost access at preparation suppresses with no provider call.

definiteRejectionCountsProviderCallTest.note: A quota rejection consumes the attempt and retries.

deliveredTest.note: Accepted then delivered by independent evidence.

inFlightPreparationKeepsObservedAuthorit.note: send does not recheck authority after preparation.

inFlightPreparationKeepsObservedConsentT.note: observeEnrollment suppresses only waiting rows, so a prepared (Sending) attempt still sends under the consent observed at preparation.

optOutTest.note: Consent withdrawn after the claim fails the preparation consent check and the row is suppressed without a provider call.

preparationAfterAuthorityLossRefusedTest.note: Preparation cannot succeed when access is not allowed.

preparationAfterOptOutRefusedTest.note: Preparation cannot succeed after consent is withdrawn.

preparationFailureDoesNotCountProviderCa.note: A preparation failure retries without any provider send.

uncertainSendCountsProviderCallTest.note: The attempt is counted at claim and a thrown send leaves the row Ambiguous within the attempt budget; provider-call counting is the attempt count.

begin.note: A registration request captures one registry read for its purpose, transaction and expected revision.

body.note: An existing binding with the same transaction and network is recognized before any expected-revision or chain check.

chain.note: Creation verification refuses unverified/mismatched creations, keeps pending or included creations pending, and only a finalized exact creation proceeds to append; difference: owner wallet presence (wallet-missing 403) is not modeled.

changeAuthority.note: GitHub authority is the external `authorized` input observed once at canBeginRegistration; it is not a lock across later steps.

checked.note: Test composition helper chaining begin through authority.

commit.note: Append is a guarded CAS on the captured revision and an unregistered purpose slot; a lost commit leaves the registration stored and recognizable.

dependencyFailure.note: A failed dependency answers 500 and commits nothing; not a modeled state.

edit.note: An owner edit appends a new immutable registry revision with its ordinary/private policies.

enforcements.note: vaultSnapshots.md commitRegistration compares only the captured registry revision; it does not capture or recheck project restriction/ban (enforcement generation). expected.note: The expected revision must exist and an existing different binding conflicts (409).

funds.note: No successor rule covers the owner vault setup GET (backend/projects/vault-setup.ts): ordinary network reads require steward/repository-admin authority and no restriction, while the private-bounty funds read stays available to a lesser authority with canSetup false while restricted or banned. history.note: A creation reviewed under an older retained revision is accepted only when its purpose policy equals the captured current policy.

omitProject.note: Project existence is part of the external authorization input `authorized` of vaultSnapshots.md canBeginRegistration; a missing project is a shell 404.

prepared.note: Test composition helper chaining writeReady through append validation.

project.note: beginRegistration captures the current revision number (capture) and the existing binding for the purpose.

service.note: An unavailable service dependency answers 503 and commits nothing; not a modeled state.

batch.note: The authorization batch rechecks that the claim is still the current registry head; a failed batch keeps the challenge consumed.

chooseRead.note: Nondeterministic harness wrapper around read; no product behaviour.

consume.note: One atomic consumption per challenge using the captured timestamp.

finish.note: Readback confirms the effective authorized claim.

foreignRegistration.note: Only the partition's actor may register.

issue.note: A 15-minute challenge is issued only for the exact current registry claim.

loseResponse.note: A lost response after a successful batch leaves the committed authorization intact.

read.note: The proof read requires the actor, current claim, unconsumed unexpired challenge and the recovered signer of the exact message; it captures the request time.

refuseIssue.note: Issue is refused for another actor, a non-current claim or no claim.

register.note: Registration appends an immutable successor claim or returns the current row for the same wallet.

requestStep.note: Harness disjunction of per-request steps; no product behaviour.

tick.note: Trusted clock advances.

completedReplayIsRefusedTest.note: A consumed challenge fails a new proof read.

consumedBeforeAuthorizationTest.note: A challenge can be consumed before authorization commits.

exactExpiryRefusesNewRequestTest.note: A proof read at the exact expiry instant fails (clock < expiresAt).

failedBatchRequiresFreshChallengeTest.note: After a failed batch the consumed challenge cannot be reused; a fresh challenge authorizes.

foreignActorCannotRegisterOrUseChallenge.note: A foreign actor can neither register nor use the challenge.

lostResponseRetainsAuthorizationTest.note: Authorization committed before a lost response remains effective.

newConsentCannotRewriteFirstAuthorizatio.note: Signing an already authorized claim again consumes the new challenge but keeps the first proof.

oldClaimAndMismatchedChallengeRefusedTes.note: No challenge for a stale claim, and a challenge for a stale claim cannot be read.

replacementAfterReadStillConsumesButCann.note: A read before the successor still consumes but cannot authorize the stale claim.

replacementDuringConsumedGapCannotAuthor.note: An intervening successor makes the read claim stale, so the batch authorizes nothing while the challenge stays consumed.

replacementRetainsClaimHistoryTest.note: A new wallet appends a successor claim; history is retained and nothing is authorized.

requestUsesCapturedTimeAcrossAwaitTest.note: Consumption and authorization use the timestamp captured at the proof read.

sameWalletRegistrationIsIdempotentTest.note: Re-registering the current wallet returns the existing claim.

signedSuccessorBecomesEffectiveWithoutEr.note: A signed successor becomes effective and earlier authorizations remain.

simultaneousReplayHasOneConsumptionWinne.note: Two verified reads of one challenge yield one consumption.

unsignedSuccessorRetainsAuthorizedDestin.note: An unsigned successor leaves the prior authorized wallet effective.

wrongWalletAndAlteredMessageDoNotConsume.note: A wrong signer or altered message fails the proof read and consumes nothing; the exact proof then authorizes.

afterCost.note: Under the held lease a verdict records the immutable draft and an unusable result escalates as unavailable; a lost lease writes nothing.

call.note: A model call starts only under the held lease with no draft.

claim.note: An unresolved dispute lacking a draft or an escalation is claimed with a fresh token when no live lease exists.

cronReport.note: The cron run's aggregate failure report after visiting every selected dispute (AggregateError from processPendingPointsDisputes) is not specified; add a run-level rule that collects rethrows and reports them after the last visit.

cronSkip.note: Skipping unselected disputes in a cron run is shell scheduling; each dispute is an independent instance.

cronStart.note: The five-minute cron is one of the claimants (canClaim by slopbotWorker); per-run selection and ordering are shell scheduling.

error.note: Unavailable project, installation or triage errors escalate while the lease is held.

escalate.note: A drafted dispute escalates to moderators under the held lease.

keepCron.note: Frame helper keeping the cron variables unchanged; no product behaviour.

read.note: The row re-read is implicit: the later guards read the current draft directly (canStartCall needs NoDraft, canEscalateDrafted needs a draft).

recordCost.note: Merged into draft/failTriage: they clear callsInFlight, which marks the call's cost as recorded; release with a call in flight records an unknown cost.

refuse.note: A live lease or a drafted-and-escalated (or resolved) dispute cannot be claimed.

release.note: Only the worker's own token releases the lease.

resolve.note: A moderator resolves an escalated dispute once; the lease is cleared.

setWorker.note: Frame helper updating a worker record; no product behaviour.

throwBeforeCost.note: A worker that loses its call cost releases its lease without escalating and the call is retained as an unknown cost.

tick.note: Worker clock advances.

draftResumeEscalatesTest.note: A later lease escalates the retained draft with one model call in total.

draftResumesWithoutSecondCallTest.note: A later lease that finds a draft cannot start another model call.

escalationWithoutDraftResumesTest.note: An escalation without a draft still needs triage, so a later lease can claim and draft.

expiredLeaseCannotDraftTest.note: A worker whose lease was taken over cannot record its draft.

resolvedRowIsFinalTest.note: A resolved dispute can never be claimed again.

throwDoesNotStopBatchTest.note: A rethrown dispute is released without escalation while independent disputes proceed; difference: the run-level failure report is not modeled (see cronReport gap).

escalate.note: Escalation happens after a leased Slopbot draft, an unavailable project/installation, or after seven days overdue, each recording the escalated notice; legacy escalated directly from triage.

open.note: Filing by the recipient of the current, integrity-verified revision creates one dispute per revision and actor; adds statement validation and the opened Inbox notice.

resolve.note: Only a Slop moderator other than the recipient decides an escalated dispute once with a reason; legacy actor==2 is the moderator.

escalationTest.note: Filed, escalated and moderator-resolved dispute is reachable; the resolution never edits the disputed revision (prose: corrections are appended through the journal), matching legacy originalAward unchanged.

complete.note: A running attempt finishes once; only a complete attempt for the current report version within its budget becomes shown.

humanDecision.note: Successor deliberately makes the assessment pure advice that no case field reads (security/assessment.md prose: 'a human decision always wins'); the human decision itself is security/cases.md decide/decideAward, so the assessment needs no reviewed state.

obsolete.note: Stuttering no-op for a late result in the legacy model; successor covers late/stale results through finish, which shows only a complete attempt bound to the current reportVersion (alwaysShownIsCurrent).

revise.note: A new report version from screening hides the shown result (shown := 0) until the new version is assessed.

start.note: Automatic attempt runs once per qualified report version; retries after failed/unavailable/lost attempts are owner runs by a current technical approver instead of a second automatic attempt (legacy cap of 2 automatic attempts).

unavailable.note: A running attempt may be recorded unavailable; a result past its budget is also unavailable in finish.

humanWinsTest.note: Human precedence is structural in the successor: the case reads no assessment field (security/assessment.md prose), so there is no reviewed state for a late result to overwrite; decisions live in security/cases.md decide.

retryTest.note: Retry after an unavailable attempt is reachable as an owner run (120 s budget) by a current technical approver rather than a second automatic attempt.

staleResultTest.note: An attempt on version 1 completing after a revision is never shown for version 2.

appeal.note: Reporter appeals a refusal or a confirmed finding with ineligible/capacity-exhausted award; records appealFrom and queues Slopbot triage; legacy two-appeal bound dropped.

approveRedaction.note: A current technical approver approves exact redacted content (target RedactionApproved) binding its digest.

award.note: Award approves (committing to a vault/direct rail or full-award hold), declines to ineligible, or becomes a related-party proposal; the legacy 'short' outcome is not created for new awards — an unfunded award commits nothing until bounty.md clearance offers a rail, and capacity-exhausted arises only from imported cases.

decide.note: Technical approver records the finding on an open, uncommitted case bound to the current report version, with relatedness declared or inherited; deciders retained.

decideAppeal.note: Independent moderator upholds (restore appealFrom) or returns (triaging, ineligible->pending, capacity wait kept); history appended.

decideRelated.note: An independent current moderator (not a prior decider) approves (commits) or refuses (ineligible) the pending related-party proposal.

disclose.note: Disclosure records only the latest approved digest (target Disclosed); changed bytes need new approval.

mitigate.note: Mitigation verification after resolution binds the deployed digest.

requestInformation.note: Open receipt moves to needs-information; successor requires a current technical approver or assigned triager.

resolve.note: Remediation resolves only with an independently reviewed exact tested patch; legacy resolve was unguarded.

awardDeciderCannotDecideAppealTest.note: declineAward appends the award decider, who then cannot decide the appeal.

capacityWaitSurvivesReturnTest.note: Return keeps CapacityExhausted; in the successor a capacity wait exists only for imported cases (ImportedCapacityWait), not from a new short award.

disclosureTest.note: Approved exact redaction followed by disclosure of the same digest is reachable; successor makes disclosure independent of remediation stage.

duplicateUpheldTest.note: Upheld appeal restores the duplicate finding.

rejectionReturnedTest.note: Returned appeal of a rejection reopens triaging with award pending.

decideAppeal.note: Only a current, independent moderator decides an appeal.

disclose.note: Only a current technical approver decides disclosure.

revokeTriager.note: Technical approver revokes a triager, audited at the next revision.

capacityWaitAppealReturnKeepsWaitTest.note: Return keeps a capacity wait; in the successor the wait comes only from imports.

financeBeforeAwardRefusedTest.note: Financial approvers read only approved or reserved awards.

ineligibleAwardAppealTest.note: Declined award is appealable and a return makes it pending.

legacyReservationApprovedTest.note: Reserved award approved by amount, readable by finance.

maintainerDecisionTest.note: Current technical approver confirms a finding.

moderatorWithoutCaseReviewRefusedTest.note: A moderator reads only during an open appeal or pending related review.

pendingAwardNotAppealableTest.note: Confirmed with pending award is not appealable.

pendingRelatedAwardRefusedTest.note: No award decision while the related review is pending.

relatedAwardReviewTest.note: Related award commits after moderator approval; successor ordering is propose-then-approve rather than approve-then-award.

reporterCannotDiscloseTest.note: Disclosure requires technicalNow, which excludes the reporter.

reporterReadTest.note: The reporter reads their own case.

revokedMaintainerRefusedTest.note: After a new snapshot without the maintainer, technicalNow fails.

revokedTriagerReadRefusedTest.note: A revoked triager is no longer in triagers and cannot read.

strangerReadRefusedTest.note: An actor with no role reads nothing.

triagerCannotDecideTest.note: Triagers may read and request information but canDecide needs technicalNow.

declineAward.note: Declines pending/capacity-exhausted awards; Reserved is outside awardOpen.

finishScreening.note: Owned claim records its observed phase and advances the revision.

legacyReservation.note: Historical reservation enters through import at receipt (ImportedReservation).

returnAppeal.note: Return reopens triaging; ineligible becomes pending and a capacity wait stays.

revise.note: Reporter revision advances screening, case and assessment versions together under exact revision CAS, open uncommitted case and draft/failed forwarding.

revokeTriager.note: Revocation is a case mutation advancing the revision.

startAnalysis.note: Assessment attempt bound to the current qualified version.

startScreening.note: Screening claim on the exact revision.

upholdAppeal.note: Uphold restores appealFrom; independence via deciders replaces the single reviewerUsed flag.

approvedObligationCannotBeRevisedTest.note: A committed award blocks revision (also journey.md stepCommittedReportUnchanged).

capacityWaitAppealSurvivesReturnTest.note: Return keeps CapacityExhausted; the wait itself is import-only in the successor.

decisionWinsReportRaceTest.note: After a decision the receipt is not open and revision is refused.

declinedAwardAppealUpheldTest.note: Upheld appeal of a declined award restores confirmed with ineligible award.

duplicateAppealUpheldTest.note: Upheld duplicate appeal restores duplicate with ineligible award.

legacyReservationApprovesOnlyByAmountTes.note: Reserved is outside awardOpen so decline is refused; only exact-amount approval.

outOfScopeAppealReturnedTest.note: Returned out-of-scope appeal reopens triaging with pending award.

returnedAppealCanReviseButNeedsFreshDeci.note: After a returned appeal the reporter may revise and a new decision binds the new version.

screenedReportNeedsNewInformationRequest.note: A legitimate, pending-review report needs a request for information before revision.

ageOut.note: A running claim becomes recoverable at 15 minutes of known age (ExactClock), replacing the legacy stale flag.

authorize.note: Grant issuance is an input in the successor (Request.grant checked by grantAllows in security/forwarding.md); the OAuth minting flow is the gap reported under api_private_authorization.

expire.note: Expiry is the comparison grant.expiresAtSeconds > request.checkedAtSeconds in security/forwarding.md grantAllows.

finishScreen.note: Only the current owned claim (revision, version, digest) records a result; a replaced claim writes nothing.

githubAnswer.note: Created -> Submitted, definite refusal -> Failed, throttled -> Draft, unknown -> Uncertain.

reconcile.note: Grant-gated listing adopts the earliest copy or, if complete and empty after five minutes, reopens the draft.

reviewRouting.note: Current maintainer other than the reporter forwards or requests information with a checked reason.

revise.note: Reporter replaces a held or information-requested draft/failed report; queues new screening and clears routing.

route.note: Routing notices only for the current qualified version, once.

send.note: Send needs the reporter grant, current qualified exact version, readiness and the atomic claim; the attempt counter is unbounded instead of 2.

verifyReceipt.note: Grant-gated exact advisory read verifies the receipt.

duplicateRemainsRecoverableTest.note: Needs-information result is unqualified and permits reporter revision.

emptyReconcileReopensDraftTest.note: Complete empty listing reopens the draft only after the five-minute quiet window (legacy reopened immediately).

forwardOverridesSpamTest.note: An explicit Forward review qualifies a spam-screened report (journey.md sometimesHumanForwarded).

freshRunningScreenNotReclaimedTest.note: A running claim younger than 15 minutes is not recoverable.

heldReportRevisedAndRequeuedTest.note: Held (spam) report is revised to version 2 and queued.

legitimateRoutesAndForwardsTest.note: Composed journey routes a legitimate report and sends it; receipt verification is reachable in forwarding.md (sometimesReceiptRecovered).

otherAccountGrantRefusedTest.note: A grant for another account fails grant.reporter/actor checks.

rateLimitedReopensDraftTest.note: Recognized throttling reopens the same draft for another claim.

renewedGrantReconcilesTest.note: Fresh grant allows reconciliation and receipt verification.

requestInformationBlocksSendTest.note: RequestInformation review is not qualified, so the send gate fails.

sendWithoutGrantRefusedTest.note: No valid reporter grant, no send.

unavailableScreenRetriesTest.note: Unavailable is recoverable and a second claim can finish with needs-information.

activate.note: Activation commits only against the revision, enforcement count and clearance generation it observed; a changed head refuses it and the project remains.

commit.note: Creation or application publication commits paused revision 1; a published application stays published.

laterRevision.note: A later owner revision appends a new revision against the expected revision.

noActivationNeeded.note: HTTP 201 response with the created receipt; successor leaves the project paused after create and activation is a separate event (projects.md activate), so no response state is modelled.

queueSetup.note: Setup check queues an admission assessment bound to the project's current revision; failure to queue changes nothing.

retry.note: A repeated creation is refused (revision must be 0; application must be pending), never undoing or duplicating the published revision.

storedApplication.note: A stored pending application is the precondition for publication by its applicant.

approvedApplicationSurvivesSetupConflict.note: A published application stays published regardless of later setup conflicts.

laterHeadDoesNotChangeQueuedRevisionTest.note: An assessment captures the revision at request and its result is accepted only for that revision; the legacy create-response receipt binding is shell.

postCommitActivationConflictKeepsProject.note: A stale observation refuses activation while the created project and its revisions remain (projects.md stepHistoryRetained).

queueFailureDoesNotUndoCreationTest.note: Creation is its own committed transition; a failed scan queue appends nothing and removes nothing.

appeal.note: Steward, listing account, banned account or moderator files one open appeal.

autoReinstate.note: Vetting service lifts only a flag-only pause with fresh clean, flag-covering scans of every repository.

clearAccount.note: Account bans are released only by a separate independent moderator decision on each account's open appeal.

completeClean.note: Clean result recorded once; it is fresh only if requested in the current restriction epoch.

deny.note: Independent moderator denies an appeal except on a pending service ban.

flag.note: Eligible flagger files; second distinct active flag quarantines a clear project; later flags only record.

moderatorBan.note: Moderator ban of clear/quarantined project, or the malice decision on a service ban that bans selected accounts and denies an open appeal.

moderatorQuarantine.note: Moderator quarantines only a clear project, fenced on revision/sequence.

moderatorReinstate.note: Independent moderator reinstates on an open appeal with fresh clean scans; account bans untouched.

requestScan.note: Assessment request captures active flags and restriction epoch.

serviceMalicious.note: Signed malicious result records a vetting-service Ban awaiting a moderator decision.

withdraw.note: Withdrawal stops counting and keeps history.

dependentModeratorRefusedTest.note: The moderator who restricted cannot reinstate.

flagDuringScanBlocksReinstatementTest.note: A flag filed during the scan is not in its snapshot so reinstatement is refused.

flagWhileRestrictedDoesNotRepauseTest.note: On an already restricted project flags only record.

flagsTest.note: Two flags pause, fresh clean scan lifts the pause.

maliciousConfirmationTest.note: Moderator malice decision bans accounts and denies the open appeal.

maliciousDecisionBansMaintainerTest.note: A service ban cannot be resolved by a plain deny; it needs decideMalice.

moderatorBanWithoutMaliceTest.note: Moderator ban adds no account bans and no malice finding.

moderatorQuarantineNeedsModeratorTest.note: Scan reinstatement applies only to FlagQuarantine.

moderatorReinstatementNeedsFreshScanTest.note: Moderator reinstatement needs fresh clean scans.

authorize.note: Current GitHub write/maintain authority is an external read; projects.md models it as the typed AuthorityRead evidence consumed by currentAuthority on each management action.

clear.note: A clean admission result recorded by the signed vetting service supplies clearance (E::cleared) for the composed project.

create.note: Composed creation records paused revision 1 under a current authority read (P::authorized requires a verified permission and an Installed Slopbot installation on the primary repository), complete skill fields, recorded license, no account ban, a free registry read and a Clear restriction, matching the legacy create guard (installed, authority, unrestricted, unchanged enforcement); clearance and activation stay separate.

fund.note: Funding is a fact of the current revision: the vault setup service's registration of a finalized ordinary vault makes the project funded (development 67fd54fd4 has no separate funding observation; spec/backend/projects.md, "A finalized owner vault registration appends one revision for the current maintainer"). It never gates creation or activation.

install.note: The Slopbot App installation is an external GitHub fact; projects.md reads it as typed Installation evidence in SetupCheck/AuthorityRead (everyRepositoryInstalled), not as a registry transition.

prepareCreate.note: The read-before-await capture of the enforcement generation is a shell detail; the successor create is one atomic composed batch whose guard (canCreate) requires restriction Clear and a free, unrestricted repository at commit.

restrict.note: A moderator quarantine or ban (or malicious result) restricts the project and in the same batch appends the paused, retired restriction revision, so it is no longer active or collectable.

revise.note: Owner revisions append one revision against the expected revision under current authority with no restriction; unlike the legacy model a revision does not itself activate the project (activation is the separate setup-check activate), and an executable change without clearance pauses it.

restrictionBeforeCreationRefusesTest.note: A restriction binding the repository (registry read restricted) or a non-Clear security state refuses creation and leaves revision 0.

restrictionRaceTest.note: A restriction after clearance pauses and retires the listing and stops collection, so the project is not active.

unfundedActivationTest.note: Activation requires authority, installation, clearance, no restriction and skill fields but no funding; P::canActivate has no funding guard, and funding is recorded only by vault registration (registerVault).

anotherRevision.note: A competing owner revision advances the revision, which refuses a removal or update that expected the earlier revision.

authorityReply.note: Denied or unavailable authority makes canRemove false (a retry, never a removal); only a verified read bound to the actor and primary repository authorizes.

beginRemoval.note: A removal request carries a fresh AuthorityRead and the expected revision (Removal record); there is no separate begin phase.

cancelApplication.note: Only the applicant cancels a pending (or already cancelled, idempotent) application or update without GitHub authority; another actor or a published record cannot cancel (the not_found/decided responses are shell).

commitRemoval.note: Removal appends one paused, retired OwnerRemoved revision at the expected revision while no restriction holds; an already removed or delisted project returns unchanged.

commitSetup.note: Activation commits only against the observed revision/enforcement/clearance generation and only for a not-retired project, so a removal in between refuses it.

enforcementArrives.note: An enforcement decision lands in the same batch as its registry revision; the composed canRemove then refuses while the restriction holds.

lostCancellationReply.note: Response loss is shell; the retry is the idempotent canCancelApplication on an already cancelled record (stepCancellationAppendsNothing).

pendingNewProject.note: Test seed switching the fixture to a not-yet-published new-project application (revision 0); the successor initial state already holds a pending application and pending update.

preparePublication.note: Read phase before the guarded write; the successor publication is atomic and its guard is evaluated at commit (canPublishApplication/canPublishUpdate).

prepareSetup.note: The captured setup-check base is the observed RegistryObservation parameter of the composed canActivate, not a separate state.

publishApplication.note: A pending new application publishes revision 1, and a pending update publishes only while the project revision equals its base; cancelled or decided records never publish.

removalReply.note: HTTP response delivery/loss is shell; the committed state is kept and replay is covered by stepRemovalReplayAppendsNothing in projects.md.

removalWriteFailure.note: A failed D1 batch is no transition in the successor (atomic composed batch); nothing is retired.

remove.note: Test helper chaining beginRemoval, authorityReply(verified) and commitRemoval; carried by the successor single remove event.

cancellationRetryNeedsNoGitHubTest.note: Cancellation takes no authority read, a repeat on a cancelled record is allowed, and cancellation appends no revision.

cancelledNewApplicationNeverPublishesTes.note: canPublishApplication requires ApplicationPending and cancellation is final, so a cancelled application never publishes and revision stays 0.

cancelledUpdateNeverPublishesTest.note: canPublishUpdate requires UpdatePending; a cancelled update never publishes.

concurrentRevisionRefusesRemovalTest.note: canRemove requires removal.expectedRevision == p.revision for an unretired project, so a competing revision refuses it.

enforcementRaceRefusesRemovalTest.note: The composed canRemove requires security.restriction == Clear; the legacy refused any enforcement-generation change, the successor refuses while a restriction holds (its retirement revision also changes the expected revision).

failedWriteDoesNotClaimRemovalTest.note: Write failure before commit is no transition in the atomic successor batch; nothing is retired.

lostRemovalReplyRetryDoesNotAppendTest.note: A retry on an owner-removed project returns it unchanged and appends nothing.

lostReplyStillRequiresFreshAuthorityTest.note: canRemove requires currentAuthority even when the project is already retired, so a denied retry is refused.

nonMaintainerCannotRemoveTest.note: A denied authority read fails currentAuthority so canRemove is false.

preparedUpdateCannotRestoreRemovedProjec.note: A pending update needs p.revision == updateBase, which removal advanced, and owner removal is permanent.

publicationWinsCancellationRaceTest.note: Once published, canCancelApplication is false and publication is final; the decided response text is shell.

removalRetainsHistoryAndObligationsTest.note: Removal appends a retired paused revision and keeps the full history; retention of Points, cases and obligations is stated in prose (other areas own them).

removedProjectRejectsPreparedSetupTest.note: Activation requires a NotRetired project and an unchanged observation, so a removed project never activates.

staleUpdateCanStillBeCancelledTest.note: canCancelUpdate has no base check, so an update whose base is stale (e.g. after removal) can still be cancelled.

unavailableAuthorityDoesNotRemoveTest.note: An unavailable read authorizes nothing; the project stays unremoved.

anotherWriter.note: A competing owner or administrator revision advances the project revision.

commit.note: An owner revision at the expected revision appends exactly one revision.

refuse.note: A mismatched expectedRevision fails changeValid, so the write is refused with no revision appended.

reply.note: No successor rule binds the publish response to the revision this request committed (rather than a later head) or makes the client's next expectedRevision that committed number; add a response/receipt rule (e.g. the reply of publishOwnerRevision names after.revision and the editor's base becomes it).

retry.note: A retry of an edited draft is a new owner revision with expectedRevision = the committed base; changeValid refuses it when another writer advanced the head.

submit.note: The owner revision carries expectedRevision (the client's base) and is checked against the current revision.

typeDuringSave.note: A local draft edit while a save is in flight is UI input; its safety (no silent publication against a later head) is carried by the expectedRevision check of changeValid.

competingWriteBeforeCommitRefusesTest.note: A write landing before commit makes expectedRevision stale, so the owner revision is refused and nothing commits.

editedDraftCannotSilentlyUseLaterHeadTes.note: The retry with base 2 against head 3 fails expectedRevision == p.revision; this relies on the client keeping the committed revision as base, which the reply gap leaves unstated.

laterHeadCannotReplaceReceiptTest.note: The successor has no rule that the response reports the committed revision even after a later writer advanced the head; add a receipt rule binding the reply to the committed revision number.

replyWithoutCompetingWriteTest.note: Without a competing write the owner revision becomes revision 2; the reply value itself is not modelled (see reply gap).

accessReply.note: Installation and permission come from the typed AuthorityRead; missing/suspended installation or denied permission are SetupActionRequired and unavailable reads SetupRetry.

activationWriteFailure.note: A failed write before commit is no transition in the atomic successor batch; the project stays paused.

attemptOrdinaryWrite.note: An ordinary owner write with a read naming another account fails authorized, so it is refused (the 422 code is shell).

begin.note: The check's captured revision is the observed RegistryObservation of canActivate; the explicit scan request flag is the OwnerRescan origin; an owner-edit check that may not activate is simply no activate event.

commitActivation.note: Activation commits only against the observed revision, enforcement count and clearance generation, appending an Activated revision; a change in between refuses it.

concurrentRevision.note: A competing revision changes observation(c), so a check that observed the earlier revision cannot activate.

decide.note: Test helper chaining prepareDecision and defaultDecision.

defaultActivation.note: Test helper chaining recheckClearance, commitActivation and defaultPostCommit; carried by the single activate event.

defaultDecision.note: Test helper choosing the activation continuation.

defaultPostCommit.note: Test helper sequencing the successful post-commit reply.

finishActivation.note: Post-commit publication/readback and its reply are shell; the committed Activated revision is retained regardless of the response.

fund.note: Funding is the registered ordinary vault of the current revision, recorded by vault setup; it never gates the setup check or activation (development 67fd54fd4 has no separate funding observation).

identityReply.note: The authority read must name the acting account (read.actor == by); unlike the legacy model, a known identity mismatch is not kept as installed-and-denied (see knownIdentityMismatchKeepsInstallationTest gap).

initialActive.note: Test seed of an already active project; reachable in the successor through activate.

omitSkills.note: Environment seed; a paused project without complete skill fields is reachable via an owner revision (sometimesPausedWithoutSkillFields) and refused by canActivate.

prepareDecision.note: The decision is either the setupState projection or the guarded activate event; there is no intermediate phase.

queueReply.note: The setup check queues initial admission for an unassessed, uncleared repository; a failed queue write records nothing, leaving SetupRetry.

recheckClearance.note: The second clearance check is part of the activation guard: E::mayContribute (cleared and unrestricted) must hold at commit.

restrict.note: A restriction landing in the composed batch; setupState reports SetupRestricted and canActivate refuses.

retire.note: Environment seed; retirement is produced by projects.md remove/adminRevise or a restriction and is checked by canActivate and setupState.

scanReply.note: Each repository shows one clearance state (Unscanned, Unverified, Stale, Queued, Quarantined, Cleared, Banned); exemption clears via grantCovers/frozenCovers.

verified.note: Test helper chaining begin, accessReply(installed, write) and identityReply(matched).

alreadyActiveNeedsNoRevisionTest.note: P::canActivate requires Paused, so an active project appends nothing and setupState is SetupReady.

changedRevisionRefusesActivationTest.note: observed == observation(c) is required, so a concurrent revision refuses activation.

confirmedActivationReturnsItsCommittedRe.note: activate appends exactly one Activated revision (P::revised); the response echoing that revision is shell.

exemptionIsNotAPassedScanTest.note: An owner-approved or frozen exemption clears the project (so setup is ready) but is labelled as an exemption, never an admission scan.

explicitIncompleteScanRequestQueuesTest.note: The OwnerRescan origin queues a new scan after an incomplete result no exemption covers.

failedWriteBeforeCommitKeepsPausedRevisi.note: A failed write is no transition in the atomic successor batch; the project stays paused.

firstClearanceDoesNotCommitActivationTes.note: Intermediate phase of the legacy two-step activation; the successor activate is a single guarded event, so no partial activation state exists.

historicalStatusDoesNotRebaseOntoLaterRe.note: setupState is a pure function of the composed state it is evaluated on; labelling a response with the revision it was computed for is a shell response detail, not a successor transition.

identityProviderFailureRemainsRetryTest.note: An unavailable identity/permission read is PermissionUnavailable, which is SetupRetry and never activates.

incompleteScanNeedsExplicitRequestTest.note: An incomplete scan is SetupActionRequired and the SetupCheck origin does not requeue it; only an explicit OwnerRescan may.

knownIdentityMismatchKeepsInstallationTe.note: setupState ignores read.actor and the Slopbot access route answers an account-id difference as 503 unavailable (slopbot/reportingReadiness.md accessAnswer), so the successor reports a retry instead of keeping the installed fact and asking for a maintainer; add an actor-mismatch branch (installed, action required) to setupState.

maliciousResultOverridesInstalledAccessT.note: A malicious result bans the project, so setupState is SetupRestricted regardless of access.

missingInstallationTest.note: installation InstallationMissing gives SetupActionRequired and canActivate refuses; the install_slopbot next-action wording is presentation.

mutationMismatchStillRefuses422Test.note: A mutation whose authority read names another account fails authorized and is refused without a write.

oldMismatchOutageNegativeControlTest.note: Negative control of the removed legacy catch path that discarded installation facts; not a successor behaviour.

ownerEditDoesNotResumePausedProjectTest.note: An owner revision keeps the paused status (it can only pause), so an edit never activates; activation is only the setup-check activate.

postCommitFailureRetainsActivationTest.note: The committed Activated revision is state; a post-commit reply failure is shell and cannot roll it back.

queueOutageStaysRetryTest.note: A failed queue write records no request, so the repository remains unassessed and setupState falls to SetupRetry.

queuedCheckDoesNotQueueAgainTest.note: A repository has at most one pending assessment: canRequestAssessment requires latestOf state != APending.

readPermissionIsDeniedTest.note: A read-only permission is PermissionDenied, giving SetupActionRequired with no activation.

restrictionAfterSecondClearanceConflicts.note: A restriction after the check makes mayContribute false and changes the enforcement count, refusing activation.

restrictionBeforeActivationRefusesTest.note: canActivate requires E::mayContribute (no restriction) and an unchanged observation.

restrictionOverridesProviderFailureTest.note: A restriction or retirement dominates every other branch of setupState.

retiredProjectNeverActivatesTest.note: A retired project fails P::canActivate (NotRetired) and reads SetupRestricted.

revisionAfterSecondClearanceConflictsTes.note: A revision after the check changes observation(c), refusing activation.

secondClearanceRefusalDoesNotActivateTes.note: A refused clearance at commit means E::mayContribute is false, so canActivate refuses.

secondClearanceThrowDoesNotActivateTest.note: An unavailable clearance read yields no activate event; nothing commits.

staleQueuesTest.note: canRequestAssessment for SetupCheck requires latestOf(...).state == NotAssessed, so a repository whose latest assessment belongs to an earlier identity (stale/not controlling) cannot be requeued by the setup check, although the prose says the check queues stale clearance; allow SetupCheck when not(controlling(e, repository)) and not cleared.

suspendedInstallationTest.note: InstallationSuspended is not Installed, so SetupActionRequired and no activation.

unavailableInstallationTest.note: InstallationUnavailable maps to SetupRetry, never a denial.

unfundedActivationTest.note: A verified, cleared, paused project activates without funding and then reads SetupReady.

unscannedQueuesTest.note: An unassessed repository is queued by the setup check, after which setupState is SetupWaiting.

close.note: An item's first close is counted once in itemsClosed.

complete.note: A completed review of an item counts it in itemsReviewed and lists its repository.

read.note: The read-only summary is computed from stored per-item activity; it writes nothing.

unavailable.note: The 503 no-store answer for a failed summary read is only prose; add a summary answer definition (like feedAnswer) proving a read failure is never a 200 with an empty summary.

duplicateItemCountsOnceTest.note: summarize counts the per-item ItemActivity list, one entry per distinct item; distinctness of items is the D1 grouping (shell).

failureNotEmptySuccessTest.note: No definition states that an unavailable summary read is 503 rather than an empty success; add summaryAnswer with readFailed implying status 503.

directRevision.note: A direct owner revision advances the revision, leaving a pending update unpublishable.

enforcementArrives.note: A restriction lands atomically with its revision and binds the project's repositories.

prepareNew.note: Read phase before the guarded write; successor publication is one atomic batch whose guards are evaluated at commit.

prepareUpdate.note: Read phase before the guarded write; successor publication is one atomic batch whose guards are evaluated at commit.

publishNew.note: A new application publishes only when its repository id and path are unlisted and unrestricted and no restriction holds; the registry claim is projectRegistry canClaim.

publishUpdate.note: A pending update publishes at its base revision with no restriction; the successor update does not claim an added repository path alias (see aliasAppendRetainsOriginalIdentityTest gap).

aliasAppendRetainsOriginalIdentityTest.note: Appending a transfer path alias to an existing project's repository while keeping its original id/path claim is not representable (canClaim requires an unlisted repository id); add an alias claim that appends a path to the same repository and project.

approvedApplicationCannotPublishTwiceTes.note: canPublishApplication requires ApplicationPending; a published application stays published.

changedBaseLeavesUpdatePendingTest.note: An update publishes only while p.revision == updateBase; a direct revision leaves it pending and unpublishable.

newApplicationWinsAliasRaceTest.note: No rule refuses a pending update whose new path alias another project claimed first, because updates claim no paths; add the alias claim to publishUpdate guarded by pathListed.

restrictionInvalidatesNewApplicationTest.note: A restriction on the security state or on the repository (registry read restricted) refuses publication, leaving revision 0 and no claim.

restrictionInvalidatesPreparedRevisionTe.note: ownerWriteAllowed requires restriction Clear at commit, so an enforcement decision refuses the prepared update.

revisionWinsAliasRaceTest.note: An update cannot claim a new path alias for an already listed repository (canClaim refuses repositoryListed), so the race where an update's alias claim refuses a new application with that path is unmodelled; add an alias-claim event for a project's own repository, refused when the path is listed elsewhere.

caseOwnerRequestsInformation.note: The case moves to NeedsInformation with a new case revision; screening.revisionPermitted reads it as caseNeedsInformation.

forward.note: A current maintainer other than the reporter records review Forward at the seen screening revision.

read.note: The client's captured CAS tokens are the seenRevision parameter and the exactCaseCas evidence of the successor events, not a state change.

requestInformation.note: A maintainer review decision RequestInformation reopens revision.

revise.note: The reporter replaces the report under both optimistic versions when held, asked for information or case-needs-information; replacement requeues screening, resets review and clears routing.

routeOwner.note: Routing of a qualified (forwarded) version marks it routed.

caseOwnerInformationReopensTest.note: evidence.caseNeedsInformation (from the case's NeedsInformation) permits replacement after a forward.

explicitInformationReopensTest.note: review RequestInformation permits a replacement, which resets review to PendingReview and routed to false.

forwardBlocksHeldEditTest.note: After Forward (routed), review is neither PendingReview nor RequestInformation, so a held-screen revision is not permitted.

forwardPendingRouteBlocksEditTest.note: Forward alone, before routing, already closes the held revision window.

staleReportCannotUndoForwardTest.note: canReplace requires seenRevision == s.revision; the forward advanced it and also closed the window.

observe.note: A refresh writes the newer observation for the project revision and repository with its enabled state and verification time.

outage.note: A failed read records ReadFailed and keeps the prior enabled state and verification time, so it is stale, distinct from a verified disabled observation.

read.note: Only a fresh, enabled, verified observation for the same revision and identity is ready; consumers read the cache, never GitHub.

revision.note: Observations are keyed by project revision and repository, so a new revision has no observation and is not ready.

tick.note: Freshness is bounded by maxAgeMs (one hour) instead of the legacy three ticks.

disabledIsNotUnavailableTest.note: A verified disabled observation (failure NoFailure, enabled false) is distinct from a failed read (failure ReadFailed); readyFor itself is boolean, so the distinction lives in the stored observation.

identityChangeTest.note: After the project revision changes, readyFor finds no observation for the new key.

execute.note: The ordered request outcome (denied, invalid, unavailable, ok) and the payment-config isolation are not modelled; add a request-pipeline rule covering actor binding, body validity and per-route configuration availability.

grantAdmin.note: The historical value import requires a verified configured administrator.

invalidateWrite.note: Exact body key sets and bounded bodies are declared shell request-hardening obligations in backend/accounts.md.

request.note: Route selection is the HTTP shell; each successor area guards its own events.

switchActor.note: backend/accounts.md declares the x-slop-expected-github-id check (403 actor_changed, requestActor) an explicit shell obligation outside the model.

validPaymentConfig.note: No successor rule makes payment configuration request-local so that malformed payment configuration fails only payment operations; add a request-composition rule (payment routes unavailable, independent routes such as sign-out and reads unaffected).

brokenPaymentAllowsSignoutTest.note: canSignOut has no configuration dependency, but nothing states that a malformed payment configuration cannot break sign-out; add the per-route configuration isolation rule.

brokenPaymentCannotPayTest.note: No rule makes payment HTTP operations unavailable (no mutation) under invalid payment configuration; operations/paymentJobs.md canBegin covers only scheduled jobs. Add it to the request composition.

changedActorCannotReadTest.note: Refusing a request whose expected actor differs (403 actor_changed) is a declared shell obligation in backend/accounts.md, outside the model.

abandon.note: forwarding.md states abandonment only as the eligibility predicate mayAbandon although its prose says the row becomes D1 `abandoned`; there is no Abandoned phase or abandon transition. Add an Abandoned ForwardingPhase and an abandon(f, idleMs, savedReport) event guarded by mayAbandon that advances the revision and is terminal.

age.note: Time is the nowMs/idleMs parameter of the successor events, not state.

ban.note: The send gate's allowedToParticipate (rechecked in the atomic claim) refuses a banned reporter.

changeGate.note: A changed approved intake/screening revision fails intakeCurrent or seenScreeningRevision, refusing the claim.

claimReadback.note: Readback must observe this request's own claim revision, request id and Submitting phase.

claimReply.note: A missing change count or lost commit response gives no readback (changedOne/rowPresent), so it cannot lend a send claim.

claimSend.note: The atomic claim needs the current revision, valid reporter grant and a matching gate; it advances the revision and binds the attempt.

commitOutcome.note: The outcome commits only while the posted claim still owns the row; a late accepted copy that lost the compare-and-set is held for reconciliation.

committed.note: Test helper composing successor-carried steps; no behaviour of its own.

contactsUnavailable.note: A matching advisory without current contacts records contactsPending and stays Submitted.

fallbackRead.note: A stale accepted reply never resends; a still-submitting row moves to uncertain via a fresh exact read.

fallbackWrite.note: The fallback compare-and-set moves the current submitting row to Uncertain.

fiveTicks.note: Test helper composing successor-carried steps; no behaviour of its own.

fourTicks.note: Test helper composing successor-carried steps; no behaviour of its own.

heldClaim.note: Test helper composing successor-carried steps; no behaviour of its own.

heldThenDraft.note: Test helper composing successor-carried steps; no behaviour of its own.

idleExpires.note: Idle expiry is the idleMs > 24h condition of mayAbandon.

interrupted.note: A submitting row older than 60 seconds becomes Uncertain.

land.note: Appearance of a GitHub copy is external provider state observed through the Listing and accepted Copy inputs.

legacyClaimReadback.note: Negative control of the removed unchecked readback; excluded by lawClaimReadbackUsesOwnRevision.

loseReceiptReply.note: A lost receipt response leaves ReceiptVerified and the linkage intact.

outcomeReadback.note: Response readback is shell; a newer row yields a safe fallback view and changes no state.

outcomeReply.note: Response delivery of the committed outcome is shell; the recorded phase is kept (alwaysSubmittedBinding).

providerResult.note: Created records the canonical earliest copy; throttled reopens a draft without copy; unknown is uncertain; definite failures are Failed with their class.

providerStart.note: A POST starts only for a claim this request read back, at most once per claim revision.

read.note: Each request carries its exact row revision; currentRequest requires it to equal the stored revision.

ready.note: Test helper composing successor-carried steps; no behaviour of its own.

reconcileEmpty.note: An exact empty listing reopens a draft only after five minutes since the latest claim.

reconcileFound.note: An exact complete listing with copies binds the earliest copy and moves to Submitted.

reconcileInconclusive.note: An inexact listing keeps Uncertain and only advances the revision.

reverseCopyOrder.note: Copy order is by creation time then GHSA rank, independent of attempt order.

save.note: Forwarding starts from a durable Slop case owned by security/intake.md; the saved case is always present in the successor (alwaysOriginalCase).

started.note: Test helper composing successor-carried steps; no behaviour of its own.

uncertain.note: Test helper composing successor-carried steps; no behaviour of its own.

verificationExpires.note: A Submitted row without pending contacts fails as Unverifiable after 24 hours; the case remains.

verify.note: A matching advisory read with committed linkage moves to ReceiptVerified and links the saved case.

written.note: Test helper composing successor-carried steps; no behaviour of its own.

banAtClaimRefusesWithoutMutationTest.note: allowedToParticipate fails at the atomic claim, so nothing changes.

changedStoredReportGateRefusesOldClaimTe.note: A changed approved intake gate fails intakeCurrent, refusing the claim.

competingSendCannotUseOldRevisionTest.note: The second sender's request revision is stale after the first claim, so it cannot claim.

delayedReadbackCannotBorrowNewClaimTest.note: Readback must match this request's id and its own claim revision, so an old request cannot borrow a newer claim.

delayedReadbackRefusesReconciledDraftTes.note: A row reopened to Draft fails the Submitting and revision checks.

delayedReadbackRefusesUncertainRowTest.note: Readback requires observedPhase Submitting at the claim revision; an interrupted row refuses it and no POST starts.

earlyEmptyCannotRetryTest.note: An empty listing before five minutes keeps Uncertain.

interruptWinsOverLateReceiptTest.note: After interruption the late created reply no longer owns the row; reconciliation later binds the copy and the receipt is verified.

lateAcceptedReplyKeepsCopyForReconciliat.note: A late accepted copy that lost the compare-and-set moves the current claim to Uncertain; the new claim's readback then fails and reconciliation binds the earliest copy.

lateCopyWinsAfterEmptyRetryTest.note: A successful resend compares its accepted copy with an exact listing and binds the earliest copy.

laterAttemptCanHaveEarlierReceiptTimesta.note: Ordering is by createdAtMs then GHSA, so a later attempt's copy may be canonical.

legacyReadbackBorrowsNewClaimNegativeCon.note: Negative control of the removed unchecked readback path; the successor forbids it by lawClaimReadbackUsesOwnRevision.

lostAcceptedOutcomeReplyKeepsSubmittedRe.note: The created outcome is committed state; a lost reply cannot undo Submitted or its canonical copy.

lostClaimReplyRecoversWithoutOldPostTest.note: The unread claim is interrupted, reconciled empty and reopened; only the new attempt posts.

lostVerifiedReplyCannotDeleteReceiptTest.note: A lost receipt reply keeps ReceiptVerified and the linkage.

missingClaimCountLeavesCommitButNoPostTe.note: Without changedOne the claim is never ready, so no POST starts while the committed claim remains.

missingOutcomeCountDoesNotUndoAcceptedCo.note: Once bound, the canonical copy cannot be replaced or removed.

missingReadbackRefusesProviderTest.note: A missing row readback (rowPresent false) leaves the claim not ready.

newerOutcomeReadbackReturnsSafeFallbackT.note: Readback of a newer row returning a fallback view is a shell response detail with no state change.

optionalDraftExpiresTest.note: The legacy witness reaches phase abandoned for an unsaved, copy-less draft after 24 idle hours; the successor has only the mayAbandon predicate and no transition or sometimes goal reaching an abandoned state. Add the abandon event and a sometimesAbandoned goal.

retryListingFailureKeepsAcceptedCopyTest.note: A failed or inexact listing yields no candidates, so the accepted copy is bound.

savedFailureNeverExpiresAwayTest.note: A saved Slop report is never abandoned.

submittedVerificationExpiryKeepsSavedCas.note: Expiry fails the forwarding as Unverifiable while the original case stays.

throttleReopensWithoutCopyTest.note: ThrottledNoCopy reopens Draft with retryWithoutCopy and no copy.

validatedReadbackIsNotAtomicWithNetworkT.note: canStartPost needs only the request's own ready claim, so a read-back request may start late after interruption.

verifiedContactsKeepSubmittedRecoveryTes.note: Verification expiry requires not(contactsPending), so a matching advisory with no contacts stays recoverable.

attach.note: Attachment consumes the intent atomically, measured at the authorization time, and rechecks ban, finalization and attached digest.

ban.note: The access-area ban is mirrored with an increasing epoch.

disableIntake.note: A disabled observation makes intakeFresh false, refusing only the byte upload.

dispatch.note: Request admission time is the beginPut authorizedAt captured in the Put record.

event.note: Owner agent events append idempotently and are refused once finalized or banned.

expire.note: Expiry is the clock passing expiresAt; beginPut then finds no live intent.

finalize.note: Finalization needs an attached trace and an unbanned owner and freezes the run.

issueIntent.note: An intent is created for the owner's unfinalized run with a compatible digest and five-minute expiry.

loseAttachmentReply.note: A lost reply leaves the committed attachment and consumed intent; the retry is refused by beginPut (ReplyCapabilityGone).

putBytes.note: The storage service writes the reserved bytes or fails; content-addressed objects are permanent.

readCapability.note: beginPut needs a live, unconsumed intent at its time (ReplyCapabilityGone otherwise).

readReservation.note: The reservation insert and its readback are one atomic beginPut; a different reserved blob is ReplyTraceConflict.

reinstate.note: A later standing observation clears the ban (sometimesUnbannedByLaterEpoch).

removedRoute.note: No route reads a contributor trace body; the trace_read_grants table is retired and no transition issues a grant.

reply.note: The HTTP reply (which may observe a later finalization) is shell; state is as committed.

reserveInsert.note: beginPut reserves exactly one permanent object before any write; a different digest is refused.

validateUpload.note: beginPut refuses a banned owner, stale intake and a content-type/size/digest mismatch; byte parsing is a shell obligation.

verifyIntake.note: The server runtime renews an enabled verified private-intake observation.

verifyObject.note: Exact object verification is folded into writeBytes success/failure; a failure keeps the reservation and leaves the put failed.

admittedRequestMayFinishAfterExpiryTest.note: attachPut checks liveness against the put's authorizedAt, so an admitted request may attach after expiry.

banAfterReservationRetainsUnattachedByte.note: Bytes written under a reservation made before a ban stay unattached and the intent unconsumed.

banBeforeReservationRefusesWriteTest.note: A banned owner gets ReplyBanned before any reservation.

banBetweenReservationAndReadbackRetainsO.note: Reservation and readback are atomic in beginPut; after a ban the reservation stays and attachPut refuses, but unlike the legacy readback the successor writeBytes may still store the bytes unattached.

banPreservesAttachedReceiptAndRefusesFin.note: A banned owner cannot finalize and the attached trace stays.

competingDigestCannotChangeReservationTe.note: A second digest is refused once the first reservation exists.

duplicateCapabilityHasOnlyOneCommitTest.note: The first attachment consumes the intent; the second finds it not live and is a conflict.

expiredBeforeDispatchRefusesCapabilityTe.note: No live intent at request time gives ReplyCapabilityGone with no reservation.

failedBatchRetainsCapabilityAndAllowsRet.note: A failed attempt leaves the intent unconsumed and the reservation unchanged, so the same capability retries; an infrastructure batch failure is no transition.

failedWriteAllowsSameCapabilityRetryTest.note: A failed write marks the put failed but keeps the unconsumed intent and reservation, so the same capability can retry.

finalizationBeforeReplyIsVisibleTest.note: A reply observing a later finalization is a shell response detail; the state transitions are attachPut then finalize.

finalizationFreezesEventsTest.note: Events after finalization are refused (ReplyFinalized) and the event list is frozen.

finalizedRunRefusesLateAttachmentTest.note: attachPut refuses a finalized run and leaves the intent unconsumed.

invalidBytesNeverReserveTest.note: Invalid bytes are refused by shell parsing or beginPut's intent-mismatch check before any reservation.

begin.note: Test-harness request construction; route authentication is the separate trace_route_authorization model.

captureFinalizeTime.note: Finalization stamps the server's current time; the successor's finalize is atomic, so the capture and write are one step.

conflictBan.note: After a refused write the answer is Banned when the owner is banned, else a conflict/finalized refusal; the successor evaluates the ban first within one atomic step.

insertEvent.note: A new key appends one event while the owner is unbanned and the run not finalized.

readEvent.note: An existing key with the same body returns ReplyExisting and a different body ReplyConflict.

readFinalized.note: Post-write readback; the successor's atomic finalize needs none, and a missing readback is a client-side stop (runEvidence stopAttempt).

readOrWriteFailure.note: Storage read/write exception answered as an error; the successor treats it as a server refusal the client stops on (runEvidence stopAttempt) with no state change.

readOwner.note: A missing run or another actor answers NotFound, an event on a finalized run answers Finalized, and finalization without an attached trace answers TraceRequired.

respond.note: Response delivery; a lost response changes no server state.

setBan.note: The ban fact comes only from the standing service, with an increasing epoch.

tick.note: The server runtime advances a monotone clock.

validateEvent.note: Only agent-source events no more than five minutes in the future are accepted, else ReplyInvalid; exact body schema is a shell parsing obligation.

writeReply.note: Statement metadata and reply loss; the successor's actions are atomic, and lost or failed replies are the client's stopAttempt in runEvidence.md, never undoing a committed effect.

differentPayloadConflictsTest.note: A different body under an existing key returns ReplyConflict.

eventReadAfterFinalizationIsRefusedTest.note: An event on a finalized run answers ReplyFinalized and appends nothing.

eventReplyLossKeepsRecordTest.note: A committed event is never removed and a retry with the same body returns ReplyExisting.

eventThenFinalizeFreezesHistoryTest.note: Finalization freezes the event history, intents and attached trace.

existingReadCanFinishAfterLateBanTest.note: Documents a read/ban interleaving in which an existing identical event is returned after a late ban; the successor's atomic appendEvent checks the ban first (ReplyBanned) and neither path changes state.

finalizationBetweenEventReadAndWritePrev.note: Once finalized the event list cannot grow.

finalizationCommitSurvivesLostReplyTest.note: A finalized run stays finalized regardless of reply loss.
