advanceRun.note: The legacy abstraction of later upload/finalization is carried by attachPut (AwaitingTrace to TraceUploaded) and finalize (to Finalized).

ban.note: A ban is the access area's standing fact mirrored by the server runtime with a strictly increasing epoch, rather than a free toggle.

begin.note: Request admission (owner as by, non-empty key) is the canCreateRun guard; the per-slot retry bookkeeping is abstracted.

committed.note: Test-harness composition of insert and insertResult; no successor counterpart is needed.

conflictBanRead.note: createRun checks the ban before classifying a conflict, so a banned actor gets ReplyBanned and an unbanned one ReplyConflict; the read failure (500) is not a transition.

created.note: Test-harness composition of a full successful creation; carried by a single createRun call.

createdRead.note: createRun is one atomic D1 decision (ban, lookup, insert under the actor/key uniqueness constraint); the separate by-ID readback and its failure are shell response construction, not state transitions.

emptyRead.note: Test-harness composition reaching the insert phase; no successor counterpart is needed.

initialBanRead.note: The ban branch of createRun refuses (ReplyBanned) before lookup; a failed ban read (500) writes nothing and is not a transition.

insert.note: The empty-key branch of createRun inserts the run in AwaitingTrace; the ban is evaluated in the same statement, so a banned actor inserts nothing.

insertFailure.note: createRun is one atomic D1 decision (ban, lookup, insert under the actor/key uniqueness constraint); a generic insert failure is no transition and leaves the instance unchanged, so a retry re-runs createRun.

insertResult.note: createRun is one atomic D1 decision (ban, lookup, insert under the actor/key uniqueness constraint); an unobserved insert result is a lost reply; the committed row is recovered by replay through createRun's ReplyExisting branch.

prepare.note: Required-field validation is validRequest inside canCreateRun; random server ID generation failure is a shell obligation and writes nothing.

prepared.note: Test-harness composition of begin, initialBanRead, readBody and prepare; no successor counterpart is needed.

raceRead.note: createRun is one atomic D1 decision (ban, lookup, insert under the actor/key uniqueness constraint); the constraint-loser's race readback is the ReplyExisting/ReplyConflict branch of the same decision.

readBody.note: Strict JSON bounds and malformed/oversized body refusals (400/413) are shell parsing obligations that run before an event reaches the traceServer machine, as its preamble states.

readExisting.note: The existing-key branches of createRun return ReplyExisting for an equal request and ReplyConflict otherwise, never changing the row.

reinstate.note: Reinstatement is a later-epoch observeStanding with banned false; a replayed older observation cannot undo it.

respond.note: HTTP delivery and loss are client-side; the client retry machine in spec/contributor/runEvidence.md (stopAttempt with LostResponse) recovers through the same server run.

tick.note: The server runtime's monotone clock observation replaces the bounded tick; no creation metadata depends on it beyond the row snapshot.

banBetweenInitialCheckAndInsertPreventsN.note: The ban is evaluated inside the same D1 statement as the insert, so a ban observed before createRun linearizes yields ReplyBanned and no row.

byIdReadbackCanObserveAdvancedRunStateTe.note: Which run state a response snapshot captures is shell response construction; replies carry no state snapshot, and the advanced states come from attachPut and finalize.

changedPayloadOnSameKeyRefusesTest.note: A different request under an existing key replies ReplyConflict and leaves the original request unchanged.

committedInsertLostResultRecoversByRepla.note: After a committed insert whose result was lost, the same request replays to ReplyExisting for the same row.

concurrentDifferentPayloadReturnsConflic.note: createRun is one atomic D1 decision (ban, lookup, insert under the actor/key uniqueness constraint); the losing different request gets ReplyConflict and the winner's request stays.

concurrentMatchingPayloadReturnsCreatedA.note: createRun is one atomic D1 decision (ban, lookup, insert under the actor/key uniqueness constraint); of two equal concurrent requests one gets ReplyCreated and the other ReplyExisting for the same row.

conflictBanReadFailurePreservesOriginalR.note: No event changes an existing row's request; the failed ban read itself is a shell failure that fires no transition.

conflictingReplayRechecksLaterBanTest.note: createRun evaluates the ban before conflict classification, so a conflicting replay after a ban replies ReplyBanned.

failedByIdReadbackDoesNotUndoCommitTest.note: A readback failure is a response failure; the committed row and its request persist.

genericInsertFailureCanRetryTest.note: A failed insert fires no transition, so the key stays unused and a retried createRun inserts the run.

initialBanReadFailureDoesNotCreateRunTes.note: createRun is one atomic D1 decision (ban, lookup, insert under the actor/key uniqueness constraint); a failed ban read is a refused request that fires no transition, so no row exists; storage-read failure is not modeled.

initialBanRefusesBeforeBodyOrLookupTest.note: A banned owner gets ReplyBanned with state NoRun before any lookup.

laterBanDoesNotUndoCommittedRunTest.note: A committed run row stays; a later ban only blocks new writes (stepBannedAddsNothing) and never removes the run.

lostSuccessResponseRecoversSameRunTest.note: A retry after a lost ReplyCreated returns ReplyExisting for the same run; client-side recovery is spec/contributor/runEvidence.md stopAttempt(LostResponse).

malformedBodyRefusesBeforePersistenceTes.note: Malformed JSON is a shell parsing obligation that refuses before any event reaches the traceServer machine.

oversizedBodyRefusesBeforePersistenceTes.note: Oversized bodies are refused by the shell's strict JSON bounds before any event reaches the traceServer machine.

raceReadFailureKeepsWinningInsertionTest.note: The winning row is never changed by later events; the loser's failed race read (500) is a shell failure that fires no transition.

randomIdFailurePrecedesFieldValidationTe.note: Server ID generation is a shell obligation; its failure fires no transition and writes nothing.

replayCanReturnAfterBanFollowingInitialA.note: With atomic createRun the replay linearizes before the ban and returns ReplyExisting; a replay linearized after the ban returns ReplyBanned instead, which is stricter than the legacy check-then-read gap.

responseRetainsStateCapturedBeforeLaterF.note: Response snapshot timing is shell response construction; the reply carries no captured state, and later finalize does not alter the creation reply.

retryAfterRefusedInsertCanCreateAfterRei.note: After a later-epoch unbanned observation, a retried createRun on the unused key inserts the run.

sameClientPayloadWithDifferentKeysCreate.note: Each create idempotency key of an actor is its own machine instance (canCreateRun admits only this instance's key), so identical payloads under different keys create distinct runs.

sameKeyAcrossActorsDoesNotConflictTest.note: Instances are per owner actor, so the same key under another actor is a separate run and never conflicts.

authority.note: Authority is by == b.actor for the bearer route and by == walletOperator for the operator route; a refused caller fires no transition (403).

batch.note: The claim, its audit record and its wallet_changed notice commit in one transition; a failed batch is no transition.

batchResult.note: Batch reply receipt and metadata validation are response-side; the committed claim is recovered through registrationReadback.

begin.note: Request admission for the contributor bearer route and the operator route are the canRegisterByBearer and canOperatorClaim guards; slot and retry bookkeeping is abstracted.

body.note: Body validity is the shell address parser plus non-empty wallet/digest; the operator's future observation time is operatorOutcome ObservationInFuture.

candidate.note: Test-harness composition of capture, prepare and readDigest.

capture.note: Server capture of observation and creation time and generated IDs are shell obligations; the successor claim carries the record digest computed by the server.

configure.note: Seed configuration of historical, registry and multi-partition rows is a test harness; the successor builds such states through register and operatorClaim (historical rows via FromGithubIssue).

contributor.note: Test-harness composition of begin, authority, body and readTip for the bearer route.

operator.note: Test-harness composition of begin, authority and body for the operator route.

prepare.note: Canonical record hashing and its failure are shell obligations; a failed hash fires no transition.

readCompeting.note: A competing root or successor means the request's predecessor is no longer current, so it is refused and the line never forks.

readCurrent.note: The current-claim read projects the newest claim of the partition and changes nothing.

readDigest.note: An existing record digest returns its claim (operatorOutcome OperatorReplayed); the bearer route refuses to append a duplicate digest.

readPredecessor.note: The predecessor must be this partition's current claim (ClaimConflict / stale refusal); cross-partition predecessors cannot be named because the predecessor is a partition-local index.

readTip.note: The contributor route checks the predecessor first and returns the current same-address registry claim unchanged (register's sameRegistryWallet no-op).

recoverDigest.note: After a lost or bad batch reply, the same-address registry winner is read back as success.

respond.note: HTTP delivery and loss are transport; claims committed before a lost response persist by stepClaimsRetained.

rootClaim.note: Test-harness composition creating a root claim; carried by one registerByBearer with predecessor 0.

stored.note: Test-harness composition of batch, batchResult and respond.

successor.note: Test-harness composition creating a successor claim; carried by one registerByBearer naming the current predecessor.

tick.note: The trusted clock is the monotone observeTime transition.

anotherActorsPredecessorRefusesTest.note: The predecessor is a partition-local index, so another actor's claim can never be the current predecessor and the request is ClaimConflict.

anotherChainsPredecessorRefusesTest.note: Chains are separate partitions with partition-local predecessors, so another chain's claim yields ClaimConflict.

badMetadataDoesNotUndoAtomicPublicationT.note: Bad batch metadata is a response issue; the committed claim stays and is read back.

batchFailureRollsBackClaimAuditAndNotice.note: Claim and notice are appended by one atomic transition, so a failed batch leaves neither; the audit row is not modeled separately.

caseOnlyLoginDifferenceIsNoopTest.note: The same-address registry claim is a no-op; the successor does not model the GitHub login at all, so login case is irrelevant.

committedBatchLostReplyRecoversExistingT.note: A committed claim whose reply was lost is read back as the current registry wallet.

concurrentSuccessorsCannotForkTest.note: Successors must name the current claim and the line stays a single chain, so a second successor of the same predecessor is refused.

contributorCreatesRootWithAtomicSideEffe.note: A first bearer registration appends the registry claim and its wallet_changed notice in one transition; the separate audit row is not modeled.

currentReadIsAnObservationNotLiveHeadTes.note: currentClaimRead is a projection at read time and changes nothing; later claims supersede it.

differentConcurrentRootsConflictTest.note: The second root's predecessor 0 is stale once the first commits, so it is refused and the first claim stays current.

emptyLineageReadsAsMissingTest.note: With no claims currentClaimRead is 0, the missing (404/null) projection.

futureOperatorObservationRefusesTest.note: An observation time after the trusted clock is ObservationInFuture and appends nothing.

historicalDigestReplayCanReturnNoncurren.note: An existing record digest is OperatorReplayed before the predecessor check, even when that claim is no longer current.

historicalSameAddressNeedsRegistrySucces.note: sameRegistryWallet requires source Registry, so a historical same-address head gets a new registry successor.

identicalConcurrentRootsRecoverOneDigest.note: The losing identical root is refused as stale and the same-address registry winner is read back as success; one claim and one notice exist.

independentChainsKeepIndependentHeadsTes.note: Each instance is one actor and one chain partition with its own claim line, so chains keep independent heads.

invalidBodyPreventsClaimTest.note: An empty wallet or digest is refused and the shell's address parser refuses malformed addresses before any event exists.

lostContributorResponseNeedsRefreshedPre.note: Retrying with the old predecessor after the claim committed is stale and refused.

missingAuthorityPreventsClaimTest.note: Only walletOperator may submit an operator claim; any other caller fires no transition.

missingPredecessorRefusesTest.note: A predecessor that is not the current claim (including a nonexistent one) is ClaimConflict.

noopResponseCanFollowAnotherReplacementT.note: The no-op reply reports the claim current when it was evaluated; a later successor may land before delivery.

olderObservationCanBeTheNewestLineageLea.note: The current claim is the newest in line order, not by observation time, so an operator claim with an older observation can be current.

operatorAlwaysUsesSolanaLineageTest.note: operatorOutcome refuses any non-Solana partition, so operator claims only reach the Solana line; legacy coerced the chain while the successor refuses it.

operatorCannotAppendToAnOldPredecessorTe.note: A predecessor that is not the current claim is ClaimConflict.

operatorKeepsClockCapturedBeforeHashingT.note: Creation-time capture before hashing is a shell obligation; the successor claim carries no creation timestamp, only the request's observation time and the server digest.

pendingHashDoesNotPublishClaimTest.note: Registration is one atomic transition; there is no intermediate hashing phase, and nothing is published until register or operatorClaim fires.

recoveryReadFailureKeepsCommittedRowsTes.note: Claims and notices are never removed, whatever happens to the recovery read.

issueFailure.note: A storage failure before the write fires no transition.

issued.note: Test-harness composition of the issue route.

prepareIssue.note: Challenge message and nonce generation is a shell obligation; its failure fires no transition.

prewrite.note: An existing attestation disables a new one, so the route returns the retained attestation.

proofBody.note: Body schema parsing is a shell obligation before the attestPossession event.

proofExisting.note: When the claim already has an attestation the route returns it before body validation and changes nothing.

proofFailure.note: Storage failures before consumption fire no transition.

proofOwner.note: The claim must belong to the authenticated actor and be on Solana.

recorded.note: Test-harness composition of commit and reply.

respondProof.note: HTTP response delivery and loss are transport; public evidence persists by stepPossessionRecordsPermanent.

submitted.note: Test-harness composition of the proof route through consumption.

successor.note: Publishing a successor claim is register/operatorClaim appending to the line; earlier attestations and challenges stay permanent.

tick.note: The trusted clock is the monotone observeTime transition.

verified.note: Test-harness composition of the proof route through verification.

consumedReplyLossDoesNotRestoreChallenge.note: A consumed challenge stays consumed whatever happens to the reply.

existingAttestationReturnsBeforeSubmitte.note: With an attestation present the route returns it and changes nothing, regardless of the submitted body.

failedBatchCanUseAnotherIssuedChallengeT.note: A spent challenge without attestation leaves the claim unattested, so another live challenge can still attest it; a batch failure is modeled as the burned-challenge outcome.

failedBatchReplyCanRecoverCommittedAttes.note: The committed attestation persists and is returned by the read.

failedCatchReadLeavesCommittedEvidenceTe.note: A failed recovery read changes nothing; the attestation stays public.

invalidSignatureBurnsChallengeWithoutEvi.note: A non-matching recovered signer consumes the challenge and records nothing.

lostSuccessResponseLeavesPublicEvidenceT.note: The attestation persists and is publicly readable after a lost response.

mismatchedPayloadBurnsChallengeTest.note: The signer is recovered over the exact stored challenge message, so changed payload fields yield a non-matching signer and burn the challenge.

otherActorCannotIssueChallengeTest.note: by must equal the claim's actor, so another actor issues nothing.

ready.note: Harness initial state with a Solana claim configured.

shiftedSignedWindowCannotPublishTest.note: The signed window is part of the exact stored message the signer is recovered over, so a shifted window cannot match and records nothing.

successorPreservesOldPossessionEvidenceT.note: Attestations are per claim and permanent, so a successor claim starts unattested while the old claim stays proven.

twoValidChallengesShareOneImmutableAttes.note: Once the claim has an attestation no other challenge can attest it, and each claim has at most one attestation.

validProofPublishesOneAttestationAndAudi.note: A matching signature on a live challenge records the claim's one attestation; the audit row is not modeled separately.

markFailed.note: A missed expectation or failed finality marks the scenario and the suite failed.

receipt.note: Finality of the scenario's receipts is read by the suite: finalized, not yet final, or failed (reorganized or reverted).

recheckPassed.note: A complete scenario's later run rechecks the same receipts and its status follows the current finality.

interruptedSendReusesJournalTest.note: After interruption the retained transaction is retransmitted without a new signature.

cancelRotation.note: Cancellation clears the pending identity, confirmation and effective time; EVM is cancelIdentityAuthorityRotation.

commit.note: Committing an award records its committedAt; Solana is commit.

reachCap.note: Test-harness composition of three bind-and-veto rounds.

solana.note: Harness initial configuration (Solana, delay 1, rotation delay 1); carried by initialize's delay and rotationDelay parameters.

solanaZeroRotation.note: Harness initial configuration with zero Solana rotation delay; carried by initialize's rotationDelay parameter.

zeroDelay.note: Harness initial configuration with zero binding delay; carried by initializeFactory's delay parameter.

evmRotationExecutesWithoutConfirmationTe.note: With rotationDelay zero anyone executes a pending EVM rotation at once.

nonOwnerCannotVetoTest.note: Only the vault owner cancels; Solana canVetoBinding requires by == owner.

paymentResetsBudgetTest.note: pay sets paidVersion and resets cancels to 0, so a new binding can be cancelled again.

solanaCancelledRotationResetsClockTest.note: Cancellation clears confirmation and time; a new proposal restarts the delay and needs a fresh confirmation.

solanaConfirmationReplayRefusedTest.note: Confirmation requires not(rotationConfirmed), so a replay is refused.

solanaZeroDelayConfirmedExecutionTest.note: With zero delay a confirmed rotation executes at once.

solanaZeroDelayStillNeedsConfirmationTes.note: Even with zero delay execution requires rotationConfirmed.

diagnosticCannotClearFailureTest.note: A failing test's primary code survives cleanup and becomes the finished status.

tick.note: Block time advances.

badImplementationCallDoesNotSetTemplateT.note: The uups compatibility predicate (proxiableUUID call) must hold; the call and UUID checks are one boolean in the successor.

cancelledIdentityReleasesCandidateForUpg.note: Cancellation clears the pending identity, so that address may then be proposed and accepted as upgrade authority.

concurrentDifferentRoleProposalsRemainSe.note: Pending identity and upgrade proposals exclude each other and the roles stay distinct through both completions.

identityRotationCannotReplacePendingProp.note: A new identity proposal requires no pending one.

identityUpgradeCandidateRefusedTest.note: successor must differ from the identity authority.

lastProposalAcceptsImmediatelyTest.note: The latest candidate accepts with no delay.

pendingIdentityExcludedFromUpgradePropos.note: successor must differ from the pending identity authority.

pendingUpgradeExcludedFromIdentityPropos.note: An identity candidate must differ from the pending upgrade authority.

proposedRecipientHasNoPowerBeforeAcceptT.note: Only the current upgradeAuthority may set the implementation; a pending recipient has no power.

burnFinalized.note: A finalized burn adds its exact quantity to burned and burnCommitted.

burnReverted.note: A finalized failed burn resets burnCommitted to burned so the same share is burned again.

claimFinalized.note: A finalized successful claim moves exactly its amount from accrued into feeIncome and the wallet balance.

configure.note: Modes are published Worker configuration; preflightPasses refuses a non-off buyback without a non-off converter and a live buyback without a live converter, matching the legacy parse refusal.

endRun.note: The pool run is a run of the Robinhood fee journal; ending it releases the network lease, and beginRun resets the per-run total for the next run.

loseBurnResponse.note: A lost burn response leaves the burn send unknown.

loseSwapResponse.note: A lost response turns the submitted purchase send unknown with its input still spent.

noteBuy.note: A dry run records the acceptable purchase as Quoted and signs nothing.

noteClaim.note: A dry run cannot claim (canClaim needs the live converter and buybackSigns), so the fee stays accrued in the vault; the successor records no separate dry-run claim note.

pause.note: The token pause switch is outside the Worker; the successor carries it as the tokenPaused field of PurchaseQuote and BurnRequest evidence read from the pinned token reader (buybackPool burnDecision/canPurchase).

price.note: Market price movement is outside the Worker; the successor carries it as quote evidence (impactBps/slippageBps in PurchaseQuote) and the finalized SwapReceipt.succeeded outcome in buybackPool.

refuseSwap.note: A moved price (impact unknown/above 3% or minimum outside 1% slippage) makes purchaseDecision Skipped, which a live run records instead of signing; canPurchase needs Quoted.

signApproval.note: The purchase pool has no exact-allowance approval send: buybackPool.purchase signs the SLOP swap directly and buybackBinding only knows BridgeApprovalSend for source networks. Add a Robinhood purchase-approval send (exact amount, own journal row, finalized before canPurchase admits the swap, allowance consumed by that swap) to buybackPool.

signBurn.note: The burn sends exactly burnDue (half of everything acquired less committed burns) to the dead address, one open burn at a time, only when the token is not paused and the decision is Quoted.

signClaim.note: The fee claim on Robinhood is a journal claim send admitted only in a recovery run with a live converter and, on Robinhood (which never converts), only when buybackSigns holds; it records the claim row and its signed reservation.

signSwap.note: The SLOP purchase is signed only for a Quoted purchase decision under live buybackSigns, to the fee wallet, with a positive signed minimum and an unpaused token; the legacy simulated-minimum check is the quote's slippage/impact evaluation. The successor has no preceding exact approval (see signApproval gap).

startRun.note: A Robinhood pool run starts only when the runtime runs and the buyback is not off; signing authority (the legacy key load) is signs(), i.e. buybackSigns requiring live modes and readiness.

swapFinalized.note: A finalized successful swap credits the exact SLOP output to purchased; allowance consumption is not modelled (see approval gap).

swapReverted.note: A finalized failed swap returns its input to the pool credit and releases its rolling exposure so the share can be bought again.

waitPaused.note: A paused token makes the burn decision Pending with reason TokenPaused, so nothing is signed.

burnPausedInFlightRetriesOnceTest.note: A burn that fails while paused releases its commitment and the same burnDue is burned once after unpausing.

claimBuyBurnTest.note: Credit is bought, half of acquired SLOP is burned once and burnDue then drops to zero; in the successor the Robinhood buyback share comes from recordRobinhoodFee/reserveLocalShare rather than directly from the claim amount.

converterOffStopsEverythingTest.note: A non-off buyback with an off converter fails preflight, and runs() is false for an off converter, so no run starts; the successor refuses at publication rather than at run start.

dryRunSignsNothingTest.note: Purchases and burns need live buybackSigns and dry-run decisions are never live; the claim is likewise refused by conversion canClaim, so the fee stays in the vault.

liveBuybackNeedsLiveConverterTest.note: The preflight refuses a live buyback under a dry-run converter, so the configuration is never published.

movedPriceRefusesTheSwapTest.note: A moved price yields a Skipped decision (ImpactAbove/SlippageOutside), and canPurchase needs a Quoted decision, so nothing is spent.

offKeepsRobinhoodUntouchedTest.note: With the buyback off, Robinhood (which never converts) admits no claim because canClaim needs converts(network) or buybackSigns, and no Robinhood conversion row ever exists.

offMidwayKeepsOpenSendsTest.note: Settling an open purchase needs no mode, so it reconciles after the buyback is switched off, while canBurn needs live buybackSigns and refuses a new burn.

pausedTokenOnlyWaitsTest.note: TokenPaused makes the burn Pending and canBurn needs a Quoted decision, so the paused token only waits.

revertedSwapReleasesAndRetriesTest.note: A failed swap restores credit and releases rolling exposure, so a later quoted purchase can spend the same share.

swapNeedsItsFinalApprovalTest.note: The purchase pool has no exact-allowance approval send: buybackPool.purchase signs the SLOP swap directly and buybackBinding only knows BridgeApprovalSend for source networks. Add a Robinhood purchase-approval send (exact amount, own journal row, finalized before canPurchase admits the swap, allowance consumed by that swap) to buybackPool.

arrive.note: A proven bridge arrival credits exactly its take amount once per network and order.

burnFailed.note: A failed burn resets burnCommitted to burned so the same share is retried.

burnFinalized.note: A finalized burn adds its quantity to burned.

buyFailed.note: A failed purchase returns its input to credit and releases its rolling exposure.

buyFinalized.note: A finalized purchase credits the exact SLOP output to purchased, which counts toward acquired.

earn.note: A Robinhood fee counts once from activation and at most half of that income is committed to the pool.

loseBurnResponse.note: A lost burn response leaves the burn unknown.

loseBuyResponse.note: A lost purchase response leaves the send unknown.

signBurn.note: The burn sends burnDue to the dead address with one open burn; unlike the legacy least(burnOwed, slop) it is not bounded by the wallet SLOP balance (see sweepSlop gap).

signBuy.note: A purchase spends the lesser of credit, finalized balance and remaining cap; the legacy buyDue (arrivals plus half of fees less committed) corresponds to credit plus reserved local share.

sweepInput.note: The owner sweep happens outside the Worker; the successor bounds every purchase by the finalized USDG balance, so a sweep only lowers the next purchase and leaves credit for later runs.

sweepSlop.note: buybackPool's burn always sends exactly burnDue (half of acquired less committed) and BurnRequest carries no finalized SLOP wallet balance, so an owner sweep of SLOP is invisible. Add the finalized SLOP balance to BurnRequest and bound the burn to the lesser of burnDue and that balance (legacy least(burnOwed, slop)), so swept SLOP is never burned.

arrivalAndFeeCombineTest.note: The single pool combines proven arrivals and the Robinhood fee share.

arrivalBuysInFullTest.note: An arrival credits its full take amount and the purchase input draws on the whole credit.

failedBurnRetriesSameShareTest.note: A failed burn releases its commitment and the same share is burned once.

failedBuyReleasesAndRetriesTest.note: A failed purchase restores credit so the same amount can be bought again.

halfOfAcquiredBurnsOnceTest.note: burnDue is half of everything acquired less committed burns, so the retained half is never halved again.

laterPurchaseOwesOnlyItsHalfTest.note: Burn is computed on cumulative acquired less committed burns, so a later purchase owes only its own half rounded down.

openBurnBlocksSecondBurnTest.note: canBurn requires no open burn send.

robinhoodFeeBuysHalfTest.note: Only half of Robinhood fee income can be committed to the pool; the other half stays unconverted.

sweptSlopIsNotBurnedTest.note: buybackPool's burn always sends exactly burnDue (half of acquired less committed) and BurnRequest carries no finalized SLOP wallet balance, so an owner sweep of SLOP is invisible. Add the finalized SLOP balance to BurnRequest and bound the burn to the lesser of burnDue and that balance (legacy least(burnOwed, slop)), so swept SLOP is never burned.

configure.note: Each journal instance is chosen once for one network (EVM or Solana) before any record.

discover.note: Historical assets are discovered by querying retained receipts and bookings by network, asset and wallet, independent of the current offer.

originalGas.note: The original send reserves its worst-case native fee against its nonce.

receive.note: An exact direct-award fee receipt is recorded once as cash received, before the award is complete.

replaceOffer.note: Replacing the mutable public offer is an external change; the successor binds recognition to retained award terms and receipts (directBountyIncome candidateRecognition), so the offer itself is not modelled.

reserveConversion.note: A native-asset conversion may sell only earned fee income less what was sold; the successor keeps a per-transaction ceiling in reserve rather than deducting the outstanding gas liabilities as the legacy model did.

secondGas.note: An EVM replacement reserves under the same nonce (largest counts once); on Solana a second send takes the next sequence number and counts separately.

topup.note: A native top-up adds to the balance and topUps, never to fee income.

verify.note: The receipt is booked as income only when the completed award and canonical chain times qualify; only booked income is the earned credit.

evmNonceLiabilityTest.note: EVM attempts sharing a nonce count only their largest unsettled reservation; the successor applies this liability to the daily native ceiling rather than to the convertible credit.

paidHistoricalAssetTest.note: Recognition uses retained award terms and every booking is retained, so the historical asset stays discoverable after the offer changes.

solanaSeparateLiabilityTest.note: Each Solana send takes its own sequence number, so their reservations count separately in the liability.

topupNotIncomeTest.note: Top-ups never become fee income and are never sold.

abandonQuoted.note: A live quoted intent left by another run is closed as failed with RunEndedBeforeSigning; the successor additionally requires it to be over an hour old.

beginCandidates.note: There is no explicit reconcile phase; an open live row of the token blocks evaluation through openRows, which is the legacy blocked set.

configure.note: The converter mode is published Worker configuration from the release workflow.

dryQuote.note: A dry run records an acceptable quote as a non-live Quoted row that counts against the run cap and never signs.

endRun.note: The run releases its own lease.

evaluate.note: Each evaluation records one outcome (no route, skipped, dust pending) from the pinned check order; Robinhood is never evaluated.

initWith.note: The initial journal plus the choice of network instance; legacy preexisting rows are reached through ordinary transitions.

observeFailed.note: A finalized revert marks the row failed with its actual fee charged.

observeFinalized.note: A finalized successful receipt of one of the row's attempts finalizes it and credits the exact output.

prepareFailed.note: A preparation failure closes the intent as failed and abandons its unsigned reservation.

rebroadcast.note: An unknown send is rebroadcast with the exact journaled bytes in any running mode; a failed rebroadcast keeps it unknown.

replaceFee.note: A same-nonce fee replacement needs live replacementSigns (owner activation), the wait and network fee evidence; the successor bounds attempts by the 3x fee rule rather than a two-replacement count.

send.note: A live signer journals the signed send as submitted under its reservation; a broadcast error turns it unknown with the attempt retained.

startRun.note: A run needs a running (non-off) Worker and a free or expired lease; it resets the run value.

convertedTest.note: A later run finalizes the submitted send from its finalized receipt.

dryRunCannotSignTest.note: A dry run records a non-live quote that never becomes submitted.

dryRunHasNoSignerTest.note: canSign needs conversionSigns, i.e. a live converter.

dryRunReconcilesOnlyTest.note: Rebroadcast of exact bytes needs no mode, but replace needs live replacementSigns.

legacyQuotedClosedTest.note: A stale live quoted intent is closed as failed by a later run, including a dry run that holds the lease.

liveReplacesTest.note: Live replacement appends same-nonce attempts; the successor bound is 3x the original fee rather than two replacements.

modeChangeMidRunTest.note: The successor reads converterMode from the current runtime in canSign, so a publication that switches to dry run mid-run stops the running run's signing at once; the legacy rule that a run keeps the mode it started with (and the change applies to the next run) is not stated. Record the run's mode at acquireLease and have canSign/evaluate use that run mode, or state explicitly that the shell reads configuration once per run.

offDuringSendRetainsTest.note: After switching off no run starts, and the journaled send and its reservation stay unchanged.

offDuringSendStateTest.note: The send stays unknown with its signed attempt and reservation retained.

offRunsNothingTest.note: acquireLease needs R::runs, false while the converter is off.

oneVisitPerRunTest.note: After a send the token has an open row, so no second intent is evaluated or signed; repeated waiting outcomes add no row (repeatsWaiting) instead of a visit-once flag.

openRowBlocksNewSendTest.note: An unsettled open row blocks evaluation of its token, so no new send is signed.

pendingDustTest.note: Dust waits as DustPending, which is not open, so a later evaluation can send.

robinhoodRetainedTest.note: Robinhood never converts, so its tokens are never evaluated or signed and stay in the wallet.

settledRowUnblocksTest.note: Once finalized the row is no longer open and the token can be evaluated and sent again in the same run.

staleLeaseRefusedTest.note: Signing needs the run's own unexpired lease.

acquire.note: A run takes a free or expired lease with a fresh run identity.

businessFailure.note: A business-terminal row (expired unlanded) closes as failed while its signed reservation stays unsettled and keeps the native liability.

journalOriginal.note: Merged into sign: the reservation becomes Signed with its tx and the row Submitted in one transition.

journalReplacement.note: Merged into replace: the signed replacement reservation and attempt are appended together.

observeFinal.note: Only a finalized receipt of one of the row's own attempts is admitted.

readBudget.note: The gas-revision CAS read is an implementation of atomicity; successor transitions evaluate liability atomically in canReserveGas/canReplace, so no stale snapshot is representable.

recoverUnsigned.note: Taking the lease abandons every reservation another run left unsigned.

release.note: A run releases only its own held lease.

reserveOriginal.note: The original reservation is written under the held lease within the daily ceiling.

reserveReplacement.note: The replacement's worst case is reserved against the daily ceiling and journaled in the same transition as its signed attempt.

send.note: Broadcast is part of sign; a later lease holder delivers journaled bytes by marking a still-Submitted row unknown (broadcastFail, which only needs the held lease) and then rebroadcasting the exact attempt, so no new bytes are ever signed for it.

settle.note: Settlement under the current lease charges the landed attempt its actual fee on the settlement day and zero to the other same-nonce attempts.

signOriginal.note: Signing and journaling the original attempt are one atomic transition bound to the run's own reservation.

signReplacement.note: The replacement is signed and journaled atomically under the held lease.

tick.note: The trusted clock advances; days are clock / dayMs.

businessTerminalDoesNotReleaseNativeLiab.note: A failed expired row keeps its nonce reservation held until a canonical receipt.

durableSendSurvivesLeaseAndMidnightTest.note: A signed unsettled reservation counts on every day until settled, and the next lease holder rebroadcasts the journaled bytes.

noncanonicalReceiptCannotReleaseTest.note: Both settling transitions require a finalized receipt of the row's own attempt.

replacementWinnerAfterLeaseAndMidnightTe.note: Whichever attempt lands settles the nonce group on its settlement day, even after a lease change and midnight.

sameNonceReplacementUsesLargestLiability.note: Only the largest unsettled reservation per nonce counts; settlement charges the landed attempt and zeroes the rest.

signedButUnjournaledCannotEscapeTakeover.note: A takeover abandons the unsigned reservation, and the old run can no longer sign without its lease, so the bytes are never journaled or sent.

staleBudgetSnapshotRefusedTest.note: The stale CAS snapshot is an implementation detail of atomic writes; successor guards recompute liability within one transition, and canReplace needs the lease holder, so this race has no representation.

staleSettlementCannotOverwriteSuccessorT.note: Finalization needs the held lease, and settled reservations never change again.

admit.note: A new intent may take a nonce at or above nonceFloor, which excludes nonces of expired unlanded sends; the nonce's largest reservation still counts once.

advance.note: The clock advances toward router deadlines.

expire.note: Only a conversion whose deadline passed at a finalized block without inclusion closes as failed (ExpiredUnlanded).

nonceAdvanced.note: The chain's nonce counter is not modelled; without a canonical receipt no transition settles anything (canFinalizeSend/canSettleExpired require one), so the hold remains.

receipt.note: A canonical receipt identifies the winner: a late receipt of the expired attempt (necessarily a revert) settles the nonce and closes reusing sends as NonceConsumed; a receipt of an open send finalizes it.

settle.note: Merged into the receipt transitions: settleGas settles the whole nonce group at the landed attempt's actual fee.

approvalCannotExpireIntoAnotherIntentTes.note: canExpireEvm requires the row kind to be Conversion.

expiredSwapCanYieldSameNonceToApprovalTe.note: After expiry the nonce can be reused by a later send while the largest reservation counts once.

lateExpiredIntentCannotBecomeSuccessfulT.note: A late receipt of the expired attempt must be a revert, leaves its row failed and closes the reusing send as NonceConsumed; the successor settles the nonce at once instead of keeping the reuser open.

nonceAdvancedWithoutReceiptStaysHeldTest.note: Without a canonical receipt the reservation stays held.

threeIntentsKeepOneNonceLiabilityTest.note: Several sends sharing one nonce keep one liability, settled once by the canonical receipt.

chooseQuote.note: Nondeterministic harness choosing quote inputs; the successor's simulation samples (quoteValues) play this role.

decide.note: The pinned check order: no route and cap/value refusals skip, dust or below ten times gas waits pending, unknown/high impact or slippage outside 1% skips, otherwise Quoted; the successor distinguishes NoRoute as its own state.

quote.note: Quote evidence is an input record from the pinned aggregator reader (conversion.md Quote); evaluate consumes it.

acceptableTest.note: A quote passing every check yields Quoted.

routeRefusedTest.note: Impact above the limit yields Skipped with ImpactAbove.

upgrade.note: D1 table rebuild migrations are storage refactors of the legacy schema; the successor models the journal row abstractly and does not model schema versions.

preservedAcrossAllRebuildsTest.note: The scenario checks that the legacy D1 table-rebuild migrations 0076-0088 preserve existing row amounts, bytes and transaction ids and backfill the kind column; the successor does not model legacy schema versions or data migrations (same reason as the upgrade action), and stepJournalAppendOnly is a transition property of the abstract journal, not a migration-preservation rule.

age.note: Rows older than 24 hours leave the rolling window as the clock advances.

convert.note: A dry quote adds to runValue only; a live signed conversion adds its value to runValue and counts in dayValue as a live submitted/unknown/finalized row; signing needs value within remaining.

journaledThenLeaseLost.note: Signing is atomic under the held lease; once the lease lapses the run cannot sign again, and the journaled row still counts in dayValue.

settle.note: A failed row leaves the day count; a finalized one stays counted.

skipOverCap.note: A quote above the remaining cap is recorded Skipped with ExceedsRemaining (or RunCapReached/DayCapReached).

start.note: A run starts with runValue 0; the rolling day value is computed from live journal rows.

agedRowsFreeBudgetTest.note: Only rows created within the last 24 hours count.

dayCapAcrossRunsTest.note: The rolling day value spans runs and bounds remaining.

dryRunNotCountedLaterTest.note: dayValue counts only live rows, so dry quotes count only in the run that made them.

failedSendFreesBudgetTest.note: Failed rows are not counted in dayValue.

leaseLossCountedNextRunTest.note: The journaled live submitted row counts in the next run's day value.

leaseLossEndsRunTest.note: A run without its lease cannot sign another send.

lostBroadcastStillCountsForNextTokenTest.note: An unknown send keeps its value counted in both run and day totals.

runCapStopsTest.note: When the run cap is used up the next quote is Skipped.

configure.note: Wallet, key and mode change only by publication; a wallet change clears readiness for the networks that wallet serves (runtime publish/keepEnabled).

holdMismatched.note: A row from a different fee wallet cannot be finalized or rebroadcast, so it stays open and blocks its token; no separate error flag is recorded.

loadClient.note: The successor models signing keys only as a per-network list and binds readiness to the configured wallet address (readinessEntryApplies), but nothing refuses a live key whose address is not the configured fee wallet. Add to runtime preflight (or the readiness rule) that a live signing key must control exactly the configured fee wallet of its network, while dry run loads no key.

observe.note: Chain observations are evidence inputs (SendReceipt from the chain observation adapter) consumed by finalizeSend.

reconcile.note: Only with the row's own wallet configured and a finalized receipt is the exact output credited.

changedWalletCannotRewriteRetainedOutput.note: With a changed wallet the retained row cannot be finalized and keeps its zero output.

differentKeyCannotControlSameWalletTest.note: The successor models signing keys only as a per-network list and binds readiness to the configured wallet address (readinessEntryApplies), but nothing refuses a live key whose address is not the configured fee wallet. Add to runtime preflight (or the readiness rule) that a live signing key must control exactly the configured fee wallet of its network, while dry run loads no key.

missingReceiptCannotCloseConsumedNonceTe.note: Finalization needs a finalized receipt of the row's own attempt; a consumed nonce alone proves nothing.

originalConfigurationRecoversExactOutput.note: Republishing the original wallet lets any running run (including dry run) finalize the row with its exact receipt output.

abandonUnsigned.note: Only Reserved (unsigned) reservations are abandoned, by a takeover or a failed preparation.

finalize.note: A finalized receipt settles the reservation at its actual fee on the settlement day; an actual fee above the reservation sets overrun and holds later signatures instead of being refused.

midnight.note: Days are clock / dayMs; unsettled reservations count on every day.

reserve.note: A reservation is admitted only if the day's liability including it stays within the daily ceiling.

sign.note: The reservation becomes Signed with its transaction.

finalizedDayTest.note: Settled fees count on their settlement day.

midnightHoldTest.note: An unsettled signed reservation still counts its maximum after midnight.

unknownNotAbandonedTest.note: A signed reservation is never abandoned; open sends keep their signed unsettled reservations.

boundaryTest.note: ordinaryFee(50) is 1 and ordinaryFee(51) is 2 by ceiling division.

oneUnitTest.note: ordinaryFee rounds gross/50 up, so one unit pays a fee of one.

observe.note: Each operator records lease-bound, revisioned, permanent coverage scans of finalized history for the transaction.

release.note: Release needs two independent operators' complete matching scans covering the signed blockhash slot, both finding the blockhash invalid and neither finding the transaction.

disagreementTest.note: Both findings must be clean; an unknown or found result refuses release.

independentProofTest.note: Two clean independent findings with matching complete coverage release the hold and retain the proof.

missingHistoryTest.note: Incomplete scans or coverage not reaching the blockhash slot refuse the proof.

inputs.note: Nondeterministic harness choosing inspection results; successor simulation samples (sendValues) cover Inspected and Unresolved sends.

inspect.note: The signer's inspection of every instruction, account, lookup table and token program is carried as SignedSend.inspection, and canSign needs Inspected with output to the fee wallet.

reconcile.note: Only the finalized receipt independently credits the exact output.

sign.note: Signing needs an Inspected route, output to the fee wallet, the signed minimum and the reserved worst case.

checkedRouteTest.note: A fully inspected route is signed and then credited from its finalized receipt.

nativeOverDebitTest.note: Native debit beyond the reserved worst case (the whole per-transaction ceiling on Solana) fails the inspection and the reservation equality, so it is not signed.

unresolvedLookupTest.note: An Unresolved inspection is refused by canSign.

broadcastBinding.note: Signing and first broadcast are one journaled transition guarded by authority == current authority; retransmission is not separately modelled (see the rotatedAuthorityCannotRebroadcastHeldBindingTest gap).

cancel.note: Only the proposer withdraws its pending rotation; the attester has no cancelling transition.

confirm.note: Only the Solana rotation authority confirms a pending rotation; EVM needs no confirmation.

delayedDelivery.note: On chain only the current identity authority can bind at the expected version, so a delayed transaction signed by a rotated-out authority reverts while a current one increments the binding version.

evm.note: The chain is fixed at deployment (EvmChain or SolanaChain) instead of a later switch; EVM deployments require a zero rotation delay.

execute.note: Anyone executes after the delay, with Solana also requiring confirmation.

finalizeReceipt.note: Legacy finalizeReceipt requires canonical-chain evidence before an attempt is finalized; signer.md canFinalizeBinding accepts any positive height for the binding attempt with no block == canonicalBlock check (only canRetireReverted and canReconcileWinner check it). Add the canonical-block guard to canFinalizeBinding/canFinalizeCancellation via a FinalizedOutcome argument.

journalBinding.note: The attester in force journals the signed binding attempt with its nonce and signing authority, moving to BindingPending.

observeCanonical.note: A reverted attempt is retired only when its finalized receipt block equals the canonical block; a non-canonical receipt changes nothing.

payExisting.note: Payment uses the latest active binding version; rotation does not invalidate existing bindings.

propose.note: The registrar (EVM) or project owner (Solana) proposes one rotation to a key distinct from the current authority and excluded roles.

reconcile.note: Reconciliation is the terminal Bound or Retired transition from finalized canonical evidence, keeping the signed attempt retained.

waitDelay.note: The delay is the deployment rotationDelay and is met when observed clock reaches effectiveAt, rather than a boolean ready flag.

walletConsent.note: The wallet's own signature over the latest intent authorizes a binding; the intent number plays the role of the consented binding version.

delayedOldAuthorityRevertsAndReconcilesT.note: An old-authority binding that reverts is retired from a finalized canonical revert and its attempt identity retained (on-chain refusal by bindingAuthority canBind).

evmRotationTest.note: EVM rotation executes immediately with zero delay and no confirmation.

independentConfirmationTest.note: A Solana rotation cannot execute without the independent rotation authority's confirmation.

minedBindingSurvivesAuthorityRotationTes.note: Rotation changes only who may bind next; an already-mined binding stays payable.

noncanonicalReceiptKeepsBindingHeldTest.note: A successful binding receipt from a non-canonical block can still finalizeBinding in signer.md because canFinalizeBinding has no canonical-block guard; add that guard and a scenario where a non-canonical successful receipt leaves the attempt BindingPending.

rotatedAuthorityCannotRebroadcastHeldBin.note: The successor merges signing and broadcast and has no retransmit/rebroadcast transition for a stored signed binding; add a rebroadcast action guarded by signedAuthority == authority so a rotated-out authority cannot resend held binding bytes.

solanaRotationTest.note: Witnesses a confirmed Solana rotation that replaces the authority.

broadcast.note: Broadcast of the journaled cancellation is merged into cancelBinding in spec/settlement/signer.md; signatures and transaction encoding are external effects there.

codeAccount.note: The successor has no notion of the attester account carrying code; add a guard refusing obsolete-binding cancellation (prepare and broadcast) unless the attester address is a plain code-free account, as binding-recovery/core.ts does.

costly.note: A cancellation whose bumped fees exceed the 10 gwei cap, gas ceiling or frozen native-cost cap is not allowed.

expireOrSupersede.note: A pending binding becomes obsolete by a newer intent (successor claim) or finalized chain time beyond its signed consent expiry.

observeCancellation.note: A finalized cancellation at the binding nonce records Cancelled with no active binding.

observeOriginal.note: A finalized successful original wins and binds even after cancellation; a reverted original in CancellationPending is retired only through the audited reconcileWinner path (canRetireReverted covers BindingPending only).

prepare.note: Only an obsolete pending binding may get one same-nonce zero-value empty-data self-transfer cancellation, journaled as CancellationPending.

codeAccountRefusedTest.note: No successor guard refuses cancellation from an attester account with code; add the plain-account precondition to canCancelBinding and a scenario.

noReceiptStillHeldTest.note: Without finalized evidence the binding stays CancellationPending with both attempts retained; missing evidence is not cancellation proof.

originalRevertedClearsPointerTest.note: A finalized reverted original retires the attempt; after a cancellation was journaled this is the reconcileWinner revert branch.

originalWinsAfterCancelTest.note: Witnesses the original binding finalizing after a cancellation was sent.

supersededClearsPointerTest.note: The cancellation winning leaves the binding Cancelled, not active.

authorize.note: Each distinct (claim, network, vault, chain, version, expiry) consent is an append-only row bounded by the 600-second submission window and 90-day lifetime plus slack.

bind.note: Execution may bind only with an unexpired consent for the current claim and version; the version increment itself is bindingAuthority bind.

choices.note: Nondeterministic input-selection helper for authorize; covered by the simulation sample values of spec/backend/bindingConsent.md.

tick.note: Time advances through the wallet registry clock.

expiredConsentCannotBindTest.note: A consent no longer leaving the submission window is unusable.

latestExpirySelectedTest.note: The executor selects the latest usable expiry.

renewalDoesNotEditOldConsentTest.note: A renewal adds a new row and never edits the earlier consent; the later expiry is selected.

versionSeparatesConsentTest.note: A consent for another binding version is never usable.

approve.note: Admission takes the committed standard direct award approval from the private case.

bindWallet.note: The authorized payer and reporter wallets are observed and the reporter consents to its current wallet.

cancel.note: The payer's same-nonce self-transfer is an external chain action; its finalized evidence enters spec/settlement/directBounty.md as an EvmRetired Retirement with lowerSettled.

execute.note: On-chain execution in payer-nonce order is external chain semantics; spec/settlement/directBounty.md records only finalized exact transfers at the retained nonce (matchesIntent) and the frontend prompt refuses to start while an earlier nonce is pending.

prepare.note: The intent reserves adjacent nonces atomically with the fee leg first (researcherNonce = feeNonce + 1).

reconcile.note: Paid holds only when both the researcher and fee receipts are recorded.

successor.note: A successor generation replaces only one unpaid leg after certified retirement, keeps the other leg, and keeps the fee leg's recipient fixed to the terms fee wallet.

verify.note: A finalized exact transfer at the leg's current nonce is recorded once per leg, consuming an unused transaction identity.

begin.note: beginRegistration captures the current revision and recognizes an existing registration with the same transaction and network, as legacy begin captures expected revision and existing flag.

beginRecovery.note: Recovery requires trustedMain, an ordinary registered deployment and no retained observation; the successor additionally restricts it to Solana mainnet (legacy left chain selection external).

observationFails.note: Any post-registration read phase may fail to ObservationUnavailable without touching the registration.

observed.note: Legacy test helper composing a valid totals read with priorRead; covered by readTotals and readPrior in spec/settlement/vaultSnapshots.md.

priorRead.note: readPrior returns ObservationOlder for an older block and unavailable for a counter regression or identity change, else proceeds to write.

ready.note: Legacy test helper composing begin then register(admitted); covered by beginRegistration, checkCreation and commitRegistration in spec/settlement/vaultSnapshots.md.

register.note: Registration is split into creation verification (refused/pending/conflict) and a compare-and-append commit under the captured revision; existing recognition precedes revision validation via beginRegistration.

totals.note: readTotals stores a finalized exact observation or finishes ObservationUnavailable (503) for unavailable or identity-refused reads; Solana additionally needs a confirmed genesis probe.

write.note: Atomic conditional write with failed/acknowledged/lost replies; lost reply still commits and reports ObservationReplyLost (503); successor compares all five cumulative counters instead of one.

failedWriteRetainsRegistrationTest.note: WriteFailed finishes unavailable, leaving registration and revision unchanged and no observation.

identityRefusalNeverSeedsTest.note: A read whose identity does not exactly match the registration finishes unavailable and seeds nothing.

lostWriteReplyDoesNotProveMissingSnapsho.note: WriteReplyLost commits the observation but reports ObservationReplyLost with 503.

missingSnapshotRecoveryNeverAppendsRevis.note: Trusted recovery reads and stores the missing first observation without appending a registry revision.

priorReadFailureKeepsImmutableRegistrati.note: A failure in the prior/write phase finishes unavailable and leaves the registration immutable.

privateAndOrdinaryStoresRemainSeparateTe.note: Ordinary and PrivateBounty deployments are separate rows; each observation stays scoped to its purpose.

racingLowerCounterRefusesTest.note: A newer block with a lower cumulative counter is not writable and finishes unavailable (503).

racingOlderBlockCannotReplaceNewerTest.note: An older finalized block cannot replace a newer stored row and an acknowledged write reports ObservationOlder.

racingRegistrationDoesNotAppendTwiceTest.note: A second commit whose captured revision is stale or whose purpose is already registered finishes RegistrationConflict (409) without a second append.

racingSameBlockOlderTimeCannotReplaceTes.note: Within the same block the earlier observation time is older and cannot replace the stored row.

recoveryCannotSelectRetainedSnapshotTest.note: canBeginRecovery requires that no ordinary observation is retained.

recoveryDoesNotSelectPrivateBountyTest.note: Recovery is fixed to the Ordinary purpose and never selects the private bounty deployment.

recoveryRefusesUnregisteredDeploymentTes.note: Recovery requires a registered deployment through canBeginRead.

registrationRefusalCreatesNoSnapshotTest.note: An unverified or mismatched creation finishes RegistrationRefused (409) without appending a revision or observation.

registrationSeedsSnapshotTest.note: A committed registration followed by a valid finalized read stores the first observation for that purpose only.

retrySeedsWithoutAnotherRevisionTest.note: A retry with the same transaction and network is recognized as existing and proceeds to read without appending another revision.

unavailableReadRetainsRegistrationTest.note: An unavailable read finishes 503 while the appended registration stays immutable without an observation.

fetchOne.note: Fetching a commit's line counts is recordLines, recorded once per commit and immutable afterwards; a failed fetch records nothing.

finish.note: Credit requires complete line evidence per commit and completeLines gates the allocation; successor gates per commit rather than publishing an all-or-nothing batch.

recover.note: Return-to-idle after a failed batch is loader control flow with no retained state; in spec/points/authorship.md a failed read simply leaves lines unrecorded.

stageAuthor.note: A late verified author link for an already credited fallback is applied by repair (a journal Reallocation preserving the total) rather than by publishing a staged author set.

start.note: The batched commit-line loader and its in-memory cache are an adapter of scripts/generate-leaderboard.ts; the successor models each commit's evidence per commit ID in spec/points/authorship.md (observePrimary/recordLines), with identity binding as adapter conformance.

completeLoadAndReuseTest.note: Once a commit's lines are recorded they are never re-recorded or rewritten, which carries cache reuse without refetch.

failedLoadCannotPublishAuthorTest.note: A late author link takes effect only through repair, which requires the commit to be Credited with complete lines, so a commit whose read failed can never gain one; difference: the successor drops batch atomicity, so a link for a different, already credited commit is not discarded by an unrelated failed read.

invalidIdentityCannotFetchTest.note: The repository/node/SHA/parent identity check that prevents any line request is GitHub-adapter conformance: spec/points/authorship.md binds every observation to the commit ID it names by construction (alwaysCommitIdentity) and has no request counter; conflicting linked-actor evidence is separately held by observePrimary (ConflictHeld).

lateAuthorLinkRepairsPriorOccurrenceTest.note: A late author link repairs a credited fallback and keeps the prior recipient as predecessor.

laterFailureDiscardsStagedTest.note: A failed later commit leaves its lines missing so the source allocation stays held; difference: earlier per-commit evidence is kept rather than discarded.

oldCacheSurvivesFailureTest.note: A later failed read never rewrites already recorded and credited line evidence.

partialLoadNotPublishedTest.note: Commits without complete line evidence keep completeLines false so no partial allocation is credited; the batch notion is replaced by per-commit gating.

blockSameWindow.note: After waiting for the same reset, a cost that still does not fit stops the collection (StopCollection).

request.note: A request is sent only when its cost fits the 4,900-point window cap and 100-point reserve (SpendNow).

responseNewWindow.note: The census Budget has no rate-limit window identity: a new window is reachable only through afterReset after a wait, which also sets waitedForReset. Add a transition observing a response whose reported reset differs from the current window that clears windowSpent and windowDrain and resets waitedForReset, so a later short cost in the new window may still wait once.

waitSameWindow.note: A cost that does not fit waits for the reported reset once (WaitForReset).

newWindowClearsConsumedCostTest.note: afterReset clears windowSpent and windowDrain so the first request of the new window can spend; difference: the successor reaches the new window only after waiting for the reported reset, not by a spontaneously changed reset timestamp.

sameWindowBlocksAfterRetryTest.note: Having already waited for the reset, budgetDecision never waits again and stops when the cost still does not fit.

finish.note: Finishing requires the terminal page and an item count equal to totalCount.

page.note: A page is accepted only at the expected unseen cursor with the established totalCount; items are deduplicated by immutable ID.

publish.note: Only a complete census (ReadyForPublication) is published, through the exact-prefix publication machine.

changingCountRefusedTest.note: A changed totalCount is not accepted as a page; difference: the first change restarts collection once and a second leaves the census Incomplete.

completeCensusTest.note: Two cursor pages ending in a terminal page with matching count reach ReadyForPublication.

completeCountStillRequiresTerminalPageTe.note: canFinish requires terminalSeen even when the item count already matches.

overlappingPagesCannotInventCountTest.note: Overlapping pages deduplicate by ID so the item count cannot reach totalCount and finish is refused.

repeatedCursorRefusedTest.note: canRecordPage refuses a cursor already seen.

limit.note: A rate-limited response of a retryable GET waits (Waiting) until the fifth attempt, after which the response is returned; non-retryable methods return immediately.

refuse.note: An ordinary authorization 403 has no delay and is returned as is without retry.

readResumesAfterLimitTest.note: A limited GET waits and a second attempt returns the response.

repeatedLimitFailsTest.note: After five attempts the fifth limited response is returned with its status; attempts never exceed five.

writeDoesNotRetryTest.note: A write is sent once and a 429 is returned without retry.

recognizePayment.note: Payout recognition is appended once per recipient/project/cycle as a PayoutReceived revision, which acceptedWork excludes from accepted-work credit.

penaltyKeepsFundedTest.note: Once the month is fixed its weight snapshot never changes, so a later penalty affects standings only and the funded award stays as frozen.

recognitionNotRewardTest.note: Payout recognition is not accepted work and never enters reward weights (also journal acceptedWork).

reverseDebitTest.note: A reversed penalty records request zero as the latest revision, so publicTotal returns the full credit.

applyBatch.note: A supplied amount is a later decision ending protection (journal decideEvaluation) and an omission of an incident-zeroed award recovers it once; difference: the legacy branch where omitting a previously batch-adopted award revokes it to zero has no successor rule (see revocation scenarios).

incident.note: Only the exact 20 October 2026 retirement batch (instant, digest, rule, amount zero) zeroes a retained award into IncidentZeroed; journal.md recordRetirementBatch appends the matching revision.

otherZero.note: Any other later zero is a later decision that ends protection (Ended after Retained) and is never the incident.

seedHistoric.note: An evaluated award recorded before the retirement instant is retained and tracked for incident recovery.

seedSnapshot.note: An award first credited from an admitted manifest without retention before retirement is an ordinary evaluated revision that evaluations.md never tracks (canRetain requires recordedAt < retiredAt), so it is never recovered.

adoptedReplayTest.note: Replaying the same adopted decision must append nothing; canDecideEvaluation has no check that the decision changes the amount or that the decision identity is new, so a replay appends a zero-delta ManifestDecision; add a guard refusing an identical decision replay.

explicitZeroEndsRecoveryTest.note: An explicit zero decision on an incident-zeroed award ends protection so a later omission never recovers it.

historicalOmittedTest.note: A retained award not hit by the incident is not IncidentZeroed, so canRecover is false and nothing is appended; its amount is retained.

recoverIncidentTest.note: Retained then incident-zeroed award is recovered to its retained amount (journal.md recoverIncident appends it).

recoveryReplayTest.note: Recovery requires IncidentZeroed, so a replay after Recovered appends nothing.

sameAmountAdoptionThenRevocationTest.note: After recovery, an explicit same-amount decision ends protection (carried by laterDecision), but the legacy rule that a later batch omitting that adopted award revokes it to zero is missing; add a journal rule (or an explicit statement plus law) defining whether omission from a reviewed batch appends a zero ManifestDecision revision.

snapshotAdoptionThenRevocationTest.note: A snapshot-origin award adopted by a batch and then omitted from the next batch is revoked to zero in the legacy model; the successor only changes evaluated awards by an explicit decideEvaluation or recoverIncident, so add a rule for omission-driven revocation of a batch-adopted award (or document that omission never revokes).

unrelatedZeroNeverRecoveredTest.note: A non-incident zero ends protection from Retained, so it is never recovered.

adjust.note: Signed adjustments are penalty (and rescore) revisions accumulated exactly by publicTotal; difference: no intermediate overflow tracking.

beginAdjustments.note: Safe-integer refusal of aggregate totals is not modelled: journal.md bounds each revision amount by P::maxSafe but publicTotal and per-month sums have no bound check before publication; add a rule refusing generation when the earned lifetime total exceeds maxSafe before signed adjustments are applied.

credit.note: Each earned credit is an append bounded per revision by amountAllowed (<= maxSafe); the lifetime and current-month sums are views (publicTotal).

finish.note: Safe-integer refusal of aggregate totals is not modelled: journal.md bounds each revision amount by P::maxSafe but publicTotal and per-month sums have no bound check before publication; add a law/guard that after exact signed accumulation both the lifetime total and the current UTC-month total lie in [-maxSafe, maxSafe], else the generation is refused.

publish.note: Safe-integer refusal of aggregate totals is not modelled: journal.md bounds each revision amount by P::maxSafe but publicTotal and per-month sums have no bound check before publication; canStage/canPublish should require the safe-total check so an unsafe lifetime or monthly total is never published.

exactBoundaryPublishesTest.note: Safe-integer refusal of aggregate totals is not modelled: journal.md bounds each revision amount by P::maxSafe but publicTotal and per-month sums have no bound check before publication; this witness (exactBoundaryPublishesTest) needs the earned-then-final total bound check and refusal.

exactSignedCancellationTest.note: Safe-integer refusal of aggregate totals is not modelled: journal.md bounds each revision amount by P::maxSafe but publicTotal and per-month sums have no bound check before publication; this witness (exactSignedCancellationTest) needs the earned-then-final total bound check and refusal.

negativeOverflowRefusedTest.note: Safe-integer refusal of aggregate totals is not modelled: journal.md bounds each revision amount by P::maxSafe but publicTotal and per-month sums have no bound check before publication; this witness (negativeOverflowRefusedTest) needs the earned-then-final total bound check and refusal.

positiveEarnedOverflowRefusedBeforeAdjus.note: Safe-integer refusal of aggregate totals is not modelled: journal.md bounds each revision amount by P::maxSafe but publicTotal and per-month sums have no bound check before publication; this witness (positiveEarnedOverflowRefusedBeforeAdjustmentTest) needs the earned-then-final total bound check and refusal.

unsafeMonthCannotHideBehindSafeLifetimeT.note: Safe-integer refusal of aggregate totals is not modelled: journal.md bounds each revision amount by P::maxSafe but publicTotal and per-month sums have no bound check before publication; this witness (unsafeMonthCannotHideBehindSafeLifetimeTest) needs the earned-then-final total bound check and refusal.

noImplicitReopenTest.note: An ordinary sign-in to a closed account is refused and issues no session.

reopenTest.note: Explicit reopening of a closed account readmits the same member (same actor) with a new session.

limit.note: A whole-batch resource-limit failure splits the batch into single-source batches (bounded failures) without loss; census.md only models cost budget and recollection, so add the split transition and its coverage invariant.

duplicateSourceRefusedTest.note: A source key that already has a revision cannot receive another first revision (latest must be noRevision).

publishedCycleRefusedTest.note: A frozen (published/settled) month classifies the correction as Protected and it is never prepared.

receiptMissing.note: A missing receipt leaves the attempt Uncertain with its hold.

recheckFinal.note: A finalized owner void of the latest root is observed and halts posting until acknowledged.

uncertainFinal.note: A successor post requires an authenticated distributor snapshot whose epochs match the retained roots, so lost canonical evidence holds the next post without erasing history; difference: no explicit in-flight result state.

canonicalVoidAfterFinalizedTest.note: A finalized root later voided is marked voided and blocks preparation until acknowledged.

changedDeploymentRefusesRetryTest.note: canRetransmit checks only posting pause and activation; add the distributor snapshot parameter and require the pinned network, token, distributor binding and gas ceiling to still match before an uncertain attempt is retransmitted.

failedPostDoesNotConsumeEpochTest.note: A finalized failure appends no root, so the next attempt finalizes at the same epoch.

unjournaledSignatureCannotBroadcastTest.note: canSubmit requires phase Journaled, so a prepared unjournaled root cannot be sent.

unknownRetryKeepsSignedBytesTest.note: Retransmission reuses the current journaled attempt and creates no new signature.

voidRequiresAcknowledgementTest.note: canPrepare requires every voided root acknowledged.

claim.note: A successful claim sets latestRootClaimed, which seals the latest root against voiding (legacy `sealed`).

post.note: Poster appends a sequential epoch bounded by live high water plus the growth cap and by spacing after the latest live root; the legacy first-root total-2 normalization is a finite reduction not carried.

tick.note: Block-time advance; successor uses arbitrary increasing timestamps instead of a bounded 1..7 clock.

olderHighSurvivesLowerEpochsTest.note: highWater folds over all nonvoided epochs, so an older higher live total survives voiding a lower latest epoch.
