floorShares.note: Each floor is the full-width quotient of pool times weight over total weight.

remainder.note: The remaining units go one each to the largest remainders, ties to the lower actor ID.

conservedTest.note: Shares sum exactly to the pool and each is its quota floor or one more.

sampledAllocationTest.note: Any valid input yields non-negative shares conserving the pool.

tieTest.note: Equal weights give the extra unit to the lower actor ID.

initWith.note: Parameterised test-harness initialiser for the run fixtures; the successor starts from monthlyExecution initial and publishes rows with publish.

pass.note: A scheduler run selects its whole batch first (the least recently attempted pending rows plus waited-on newer v2 roots), then stamps and submits each row in turn, newest period first, each independently; the successor splits the pass into per-row select, mark and submit steps.

passAny.note: Nondeterministic wrapper choosing executor failures for runPass; the successor models failure per row as SendResult Failed in monthlyExecution submit.

reattest.note: A fresh EVM V2 attempt is appended when the latest attempt's source sequence differs from the finalized view (0083 reattestation); earlier attempts are retained.

runPass.note: Newest-first ordering is carried as an in-run guard: a batch row is attempted and submitted only after every newer pending row of the batch was processed. Under the stated sameSignerNonceOrder assumption an unadmitted newer v2 root sent while an older step of its vault is in flight lands after it and reverts (reorderedBy); canSubmit refuses that send, so across runs the newer root waits until the older send's finality is observed.

runPassOldestFirst.note: Counter-example ordering that is never part of step; the successor excludes it within a run by the newest-first canMarkAttempt/newerRootPending guard and across runs by the canSubmit refusal of a reordered root send (reorderedBy under sameSignerNonceOrder), and states the consequence as alwaysNoReorderingRevert in monthlyExecution.

tick.note: Closing the commitment window refuses an unadmitted month (WindowClosedUnadmitted); an admitted month stays resumable via canComplete.

closedWindowNotAdmittedTest.note: No attempt is admitted after the window closes; the unadmitted month is refused and funds stay free.

completeOnlyAfterLeavesTest.note: An admitted month completes only once finalized evidence shows no remaining pool gross, i.e. after every leaf is materialized; window closure does not complete it.

legacyCompletesOnSecondPassTest.note: A retained V1 root admits the month with every leaf committed at once, and completion follows from finalized zero remainder; the successor does not model the two-pass cursor.

newestFirstReservesBeforeOlderLeafTest.note: The newer v2 root is submitted and completes while the older row waits, witnessed by sometimesNewestFirst.

oldestFirstRevertsReservationTest.note: The successor keeps the revert mechanics: a root send that an older in-flight step of its vault precedes is invalidated (reorderedBy) and its landing counts a revert in observeFinality. The newest-first run order and the canSubmit refusal of such a send make the oldest-first revert unreachable, asserted by alwaysNoReorderingRevert rather than demonstrated as a counter-example.

prerequisiteAddedForLruCandidateTest.note: An omitted newer v2 root of the same vault that a selected older row waits on is added to the run's batch as a prerequisite and attempted before the older row.

prerequisiteFailureStillRunsOriginalTest.note: A failed newer-root prerequisite is processed in the run (SendResult Failed), so newerRootPending no longer blocks the original older row, which is then attempted and submitted in the same run; while that older send is in flight a later run refuses to send the newer root (reorderedBy), and the newer root is reattested via monthlyCommitment signEvm.

raceRun.note: Fixture prefix (older admitted V2 month with a leaf left, current V2 month unadmitted) without its own expectation; its continuations are mapped individually.

ban.note: Active moderator bans are an input read at obligation creation and exclude the banned account's share; a later ban never removes a created obligation.

check.note: The read phase is merged with the write into one atomic creation guarded by fresh coverage; underfunded months create nothing and record a notice.

cutoff.note: Time is observed explicitly; the closed month gates the proposal (and hence any freeze) and the 72-hour cutoff gates the automatic freeze.

deposit.note: Deposits into the project vault raise its free balance via escrow deposit.

disable.note: The month observes the project's automatic setting change (set in monthlySettings setAutomatic); turning the default off is always accepted.

freeze.note: Exactly one freeze with its trigger; the owner path ignores the automatic default while the automatic path requires it (or a pledge) and the cutoff.

load.note: The month observes the current registry revision and the owner path requires an authority fact bound to the observed revision, replacing the loadedRevision == revision check.

pause.note: A pause is observed as a new eligibility revision; the automatic freeze refuses a paused project unless pledged, but unlike development the owner's canFinalize is not gated on an active project, only on the revision-bound authority fact.

refresh.note: The coordinator accepts a finalized vault observation only when fresh (no older than 30 minutes) at obligation creation; the background snapshot job that refreshes it is the supplier of that typed input, and snapshot versions are not modelled.

reserve.note: The chain reservation of the month's unreserved obligations debits free funds only when free covers the remainder, as escrow canAdmitRoot requires.

write.note: The compare-and-set write is abstracted by the atomic createObligations transition; see concurrentMonthsFencedTest for the cross-month fence that is not modelled.

bannedBeforeCreationExcludedTest.note: A ban read at creation excludes that share and records the exact ban; an all-excluded month completes with no obligation.

concurrentMonthsFencedTest.note: The successor instance is one month and takes earlierUnreserved as a free input, so two months of the same vault can both pass covered from the same observation; add a composed rule (in monthly or monthlySettlement) that obligation creation is fenced by the vault's monthly-obligation count, chain-obligation count and snapshot identity, so the second concurrent write misses and retries.

fundedBanDoesNotEraseTest.note: A ban after creation never removes or shrinks a created obligation.

openMonthRefusedTest.note: A month cannot be proposed before it ends, and finalize requires a Proposed month, so no freeze happens while the month is open.

ownerFreezeIgnoresAutomaticTest.note: The owner may finalize a month after turning the automatic default off.

refreshedSnapshotMissesTest.note: The successor evaluates freshness and coverage atomically at creation, so the check-then-refresh race of the legacy CAS cannot occur; the miss-and-retry is abstracted.

registryRaceTest.note: A concurrent registry change refuses the owner freeze because the authority fact must match the observed eligibility revision; the successor does not additionally refuse an owner finalization only because the project is paused.

secondMonthNeedsBothTest.note: Coverage requires free funds for this month's payable total plus every earlier unreserved obligation (earlierUnreserved); binding that input to the earlier month is an input obligation.

settingsRaceTest.note: With the default turned off (and no pledge) the automatic freeze is refused.

staleSnapshotOvercommitTest.note: A 30-minute-fresh observation may still predate a reservation so an obligation can be premature off chain; the contract still refuses the over-reservation (escrow canAdmitRoot free >= remainder), but the successor does not state this bounded overcommit explicitly.

underfundedWaitTest.note: An underfunded frozen month creates no obligation and records one Inbox exception, then funds later.

commit.note: A change commits only while Proposed and not (automatic and now >= cutoff), read at the write.

cutoff.note: The clock passing the 72-hour cutoff is an observed time step.

disable.note: The month observes the setting turned off (setAutomatic in monthlySettings).

enable.note: The month observes the setting turned on; the successor additionally refuses turning it on while a cut's notice outlasts the cutoff.

freeze.note: The automatic freeze at the cutoff with the default on.

queueWrite.note: Request receipt before the SQL write; the successor evaluates setting and clock atomically in the adjust/cut guard (changeAllowed) at the write itself, so the queued phase is not modelled.

refuse.note: Refusal is the negation of the changeAllowed guard (frozen month or automatic default after cutoff); no refusal record is modelled.

beforeCutoffCommitTest.note: A change before the cutoff commits.

currentOptInRejectsLateEditTest.note: Turning the default back on before the write makes the late change refuse.

currentOptOutAllowsLateEditTest.note: With the current default off, a change after the cutoff commits.

frozenMonthRejectsEditTest.note: A frozen month refuses every change even after the default is turned off.

queuedAcrossCutoffTest.note: The guard is evaluated at the write, so a change requested before the cutoff but written after it with the default on is refused.

admit.note: A finalized admitted root equal to any retained signed attempt admits the month.

disable.note: Owner opt-out appears in the finalized view (monthlyEnabled false); escrow canAdmitRoot refuses admission while off, and an admitted month remains resumable.

materialize.note: A proven leaf of the admitted root reserves exactly one obligation, also after opt-out.

publish.note: A new attempt is appended for the same frozen month only before admission; it cannot change the frozen allocation.

alreadyAdmittedNoReplacementTest.note: No attempt is signed once a root is admitted.

oldAttemptWinsTest.note: An earlier retained attempt may still win admission after a later reattestation, and leaves then materialize after opt-out.

rootMutationRejectedTest.note: The first authorization fixes the frozen month; attempts sign only remaining leaves of that month, so a different allocation root cannot be published.

banActor.note: The ban is read again at the write boundary through the authority fact; monthlySettings mayChange applies the same rule to setting changes.

begin.note: Authorization read before the SQL execution; the successor carries what it observed as the AuthorityFact/SettingsAuthority and expectedSequence parameters of adjust, cut and setAutomatic, rechecked at the write.

changeProject.note: A new registry revision is observed and an authority fact bound to the old revision no longer manages the month.

cutoff.note: Time passing the cutoff is observed.

execute.note: The allocation mutation commits only with current authority, sequence, unfrozen month and no automatic cutoff; the enable/disable mutations are monthlySettings canSetAutomatic. Refusal codes are not modelled.

freeze.note: Freezing moves the month out of Proposed so later changes refuse.

loseRegistry.note: An unavailable registry yields no current typed authority fact, so no guarded transition fires; the payment_registry_unavailable refusal code is a shell detail.

otherAllocation.note: A competing allocation change increments the month sequence so a stale expectedSequence refuses.

otherOptOut.note: A competing setting change appends the next sequence.

allocationCutoffStillRefusesTest.note: With the default on, an allocation change after the cutoff refuses.

allocationRefusesChangedAuthorityTest.note: An authority fact for an older eligibility revision refuses the allocation write (refusal code not modelled).

competingAllocationStillRefusesTest.note: A stale expectedSequence after a competing change refuses.

currentAllocationCommitsTest.note: A current allocation change commits and increments the sequence.

currentEnableCommitsTest.note: A current enable commits and appends the next setting sequence.

currentOffAllowsAllocationAfterCutoffTes.note: With the current default off a change after the cutoff commits.

cutoffPrecedesCompetingAllocationRefusal.note: Same missing refusal precedence: a write after both a competing change and the cutoff must report cutoff_passed; add the typed refusal reason ordering to the adjust guard.

cutoffPrecedesFrozenMonthRefusalTest.note: The successor refuses the write but models no refusal reason, so the API contract that cutoff_passed takes precedence over allocations_changed for a frozen month is lost; add a typed adjust refusal reason with the development precedence (registry, project_changed, account_banned, cutoff_passed, allocations_changed).

delayedEnableCannotOvertakeOptOutTest.note: An enable carrying a stale expectedSequence refuses after a concurrent opt-out.

disableRefusesChangedAuthorityTest.note: Disabling is likewise refused under a stale revision.

enableRefusesChangedAuthorityTest.note: A setting change authorized against an older revision is refused once the newer revision is observed.

explicitOffCanFollowAnotherOffTest.note: Development lets an explicit disable commit even when another change advanced the setting sequence (turning off is always safe), but monthlySettings canSetAutomatic requires expectedSequence == sequence for every change; add a rule that a disable ignores the read sequence (only enable is sequence-checked).

frozenMonthStillRefusesTest.note: A frozen month refuses allocation changes.

missingRegistryRefusesMutationTest.note: An unavailable registry provides no current authority input, so no mutation transition is enabled; the specific payment_registry_unavailable code is a shell refusal detail.

newBanStillRefusesTest.note: A ban read at the write refuses the setting change.

unchangedPausedProjectMayUpdateSettingTe.note: Setting changes are not gated on project pause, only on current authority and revision.

authorize.note: The attester approves only fresh checked wrong-total untouched evidence; the owner separately signs the release.

inspect.note: The owner request, freshness, root match and wrong-total facts are checked against the retained allocation at the latest observed finalized height.

inspectAny.note: Nondeterministic wrapper over inspect; successor samples evidence via its simulation value sets.

materialize.note: Settling any part of the reserve marks it touched and drops any pending review.

release.note: Finalized release returns the whole untouched reserve to free funds.

healthyRefusedTest.note: canCheck refuses when the allocation total equals the reserve (healthy).

touchedRefusedTest.note: Any partial settlement makes the reserve touched and canCheck/canApprove refuse.

wrongTotalReleaseTest.note: A wrong-total untouched reserve with current owner request and fresh evidence is released whole.

admit.note: Admission requires the owner opt-in, an open window and free funds covering the remainder, moving them into the pool reserve.

closeWindow.note: The admission window is a function of the period and the chain clock rather than a separate flag.

disable.note: The owner turns the monthly opt-in off on chain.

leaf.note: Each proven leaf moves its gross from pending to a reserved award once (source must be free).

pay.note: Paying a reserved award moves its gross to paid.

closedAdmissionTest.note: No root is admitted outside the window.

duplicateLeafTest.note: A leaf whose source already holds an award is refused.

optOutPreservesFundedTest.note: Leaves of an admitted root still materialize and pay after opt-out and window close.

choices.note: Nondeterministic wrapper over inspect inputs; successor samples via simulation values.

classify.note: A matching existing award reserves the obligation; a different actor or gross marks it conflicted.

inspect.note: The coordinator reads the finalized award under the obligation's source key; matching compares actor and gross (fee is derived from the vault purpose in escrow, so a separate fee mismatch is not representable).

reserve.note: Reservation needs free funds covering the admitted remainder; on Solana the remainder must equal the whole gross.

differentActorRefusedTest.note: An existing award with another actor makes the obligation conflicted and never reserved by this month.

evmMatchingNeedsNoNewFundsTest.note: An identical existing award reserves the obligation with no new funds; the signed remainder then excludes it.

solanaWholeMonthNeedsFundsTest.note: Solana admission requires remainingGross == wholeGross and free funds for it, so an existing award does not reduce the funds needed; monthlyCommitment signSolana additionally refuses a month with an already-consumed source.

classify.note: Historical prior-cycle carry computation is retired for new months: CLAUDE.md says historical cycles keep their original windows and terms and rollover never increases a later monthly cap, and spec/settlement/monthly.md canPropose sizes each month from the revision's fixed monthlyAmount (unallocated funds never raise a later month).

inspect.note: Historical prior-cycle carry computation is retired for new months: CLAUDE.md says historical cycles keep their original windows and terms and rollover never increases a later monthly cap, and spec/settlement/monthly.md canPropose sizes each month from the revision's fixed monthlyAmount (unallocated funds never raise a later month).

approvedStaysOriginalCycleTest.note: Historical prior-cycle carry computation is retired for new months: CLAUDE.md says historical cycles keep their original windows and terms and rollover never increases a later monthly cap, and spec/settlement/monthly.md canPropose sizes each month from the revision's fixed monthlyAmount (unallocated funds never raise a later month).

lapsePreservesSharedPoolTest.note: Historical prior-cycle carry computation is retired for new months: CLAUDE.md says historical cycles keep their original windows and terms and rollover never increases a later monthly cap, and spec/settlement/monthly.md canPropose sizes each month from the revision's fixed monthlyAmount (unallocated funds never raise a later month).

lateApprovalNotAsOfTest.note: Historical prior-cycle carry computation is retired for new months: CLAUDE.md says historical cycles keep their original windows and terms and rollover never increases a later monthly cap, and spec/settlement/monthly.md canPropose sizes each month from the revision's fixed monthlyAmount (unallocated funds never raise a later month).

noSyntheticTrialMoneyTest.note: Historical prior-cycle carry computation is retired for new months: CLAUDE.md says historical cycles keep their original windows and terms and rollover never increases a later monthly cap, and spec/settlement/monthly.md canPropose sizes each month from the revision's fixed monthlyAmount (unallocated funds never raise a later month).

allocate.note: The first five distinct reviewers share a pool capped by the assessment in ten-Point largest-remainder units.

chooseSize.note: The PR's assessed value sets the review pool cap; the successor restricts it to published size bands of at least 10 Points.

ingest.note: Qualifying reviews are recorded once per actor, raising a retained reviewer's band without changing tie priority.

produce.note: Composite harness sequence for sampledReviewTest; successor uses simulation value sets.

duplicateSourceRefusedTest.note: A repeated review of the same actor never adds a second reviewer; a reused review id with another actor is refused.

minimumPoolTest.note: A reviewed PR always has a pool of at least one ten-Point unit because assessments are size bands >= 10 (the legacy zero-size floor of one credit unit is replaced).

sampledReviewTest.note: Random ingestion keeps at most five distinct credited reviewers.

unorderedHighestBandTest.note: Out-of-order ingestion restarts the record and the adapter resupplies reviews in order, yielding the same first five and highest bands; the successor makes ordering an adapter obligation instead of accepting any order.

identify.note: A reading for another network or asset (chain id/genesis mismatch) is never verified.

invalid.note: A token the chain refuses is never verified, so the asset is refused.

metadata.note: Decimals come from the chain read and must be within 36; the optional symbol is display data outside the verified reading.

native.note: Prose says a native coin or listed stablecoin takes the network's fixed decimals without any RPC read, but no definition carries that path (assetVerified requires a ChainReadDone reading); add a rule that a native/listed-stablecoin asset is verified from the network definition with no chain read.

request.note: The RPC request is an external shell effect of the project API; the bounded attempt count is not modelled.

store.note: The registry accepts the asset only after the chain reading verifies it.

unavailable.note: The successor only says an unreachable read is not verified (lawUnreadAssetIsRefused); it has no definition distinguishing a retryable unreachable or rate-limited read (503) from a refused asset (422); add a classification rule that ChainReadUnreachable yields retry and never refusal.

malformedAssetRefusedTest.note: A refused chain read never verifies the asset, so nothing is stored.

nativeNoRpcTest.note: The no-RPC native path is prose only; add a definition verifying a native or listed-stablecoin asset from fixed network decimals without a chain read.

optionalSymbolPreservedTest.note: The symbol is display data: rewardAsset.md states an unreadable symbol keeps the maintainer's display symbol and AssetReading deliberately carries only network, asset and decimals.

rateLimitRetriesTest.note: No rule makes an unreachable/rate-limited read retryable and a later successful read verify the asset; add the retry classification for ChainReadUnreachable.

wrongNetworkCannotPublishTest.note: A reading for another network is never verified.

prove.note: Each submitted file must replay onto the accepted parent to the exact accepted bytes; the successor reasons per file rather than per path batch.

returnComplete.note: A replay counts only when every submitted path replayed and held.

completeBatchesReturnTest.note: All files replayed and held make the proof complete.

firstBatchIsNotCompleteProofTest.note: replayComplete requires replayed.length() == submittedPaths, so a partial set is not a proof.

laterFailureDiscardsProofTest.note: One failed file discards the whole replay proof.

addLeft.note: Left-half PR ids of a split over-limit query; the successor counts ids per half rather than accumulating them.

addRight.note: Right-half PR ids of a split over-limit query.

combine.note: Halves combine only when disjoint and their counts sum to the parent count.

finishLeft.note: A half finishes only when its pages are complete with fresh cursors.

finishRight.note: A half finishes only when its pages are complete with fresh cursors.

movingCount.note: An unstable issue count (countsStable false) makes the census incomplete.

completePartitionTest.note: Disjoint halves summing to the parent count form complete coverage.

deadline.note: An appeal unresolved seven days after opening becomes due and is queued.

escalate.note: Escalation happens by published criteria, draft rejection or overdue dispatch, notifying moderators; the successor records the escalation reason.

maintainerReopen.note: A verified maintainer reopen of the revision resolves the appeal upheld, even after escalation.

open.note: The author opens one appeal per item revision.

publish.note: The resolution comment is posted once after resolution.

recordDraft.note: Slopbot stores the first draft with its confidence.

replay.note: A retried resolution resumes recorded writes without reposting or changing the resolution.

resolve.note: An unescalated draft is accepted by the appellant or a current maintainer (resolution follows the draft) and an escalated appeal is decided only by a moderator other than the appellant; the successor no longer lets a maintainer resolve against the draft.

appealReversalTest.note: An accepted uphold draft resolves the appeal upheld and is posted; the debit reversal is applied by the penalty journal (points/penalties.md AppealUpheld) through the Slopbot composition.

escalatedCommandNeedsModeratorTest.note: An escalated appeal ignores draft answers and only a moderator decides it.

escalatedReviewTest.note: An overdue appeal escalates and a moderator denies it, leaving the debit standing.

independentMaintainerReopenTest.note: A maintainer reopen resolves an escalated appeal as upheld.

complete.note: Finishing a live slot as SlotCompleted occupies it for one day; the legacy clearing of pendingClose is instead done by settleClose.

definitiveRefusal.note: settleClose(confirmed=false) records CloseRejected, which no longer occupies the slot; the guard does not distinguish uncertain sends because definitive refusal evidence comes from close capacity.

dispatchClose.note: Reserving a close on the live slot marks it ClosePending, which occupies the slot regardless of claim status or time.

expire.note: Lease expiry is modelled by elapsing time past leaseUntil, after which occupies() no longer counts a running slot unless a close is pending.

failReview.note: Finishing a live slot as SlotFailed frees it unless its close mark is ClosePending; the legacy uncertain flag is represented by the retained ClosePending mark.

reconcile.note: settleClose(confirmed=true) turns a pending close into CloseConfirmed, which occupies the slot for a day after the close, so a confirmed close counts once.

start.note: A new author's review claims a slot only while fewer than three other reviews occupy slots (running unexpired, completed within a day, pending close); an expired or failed own slot is restartable unless its close is pending.

verifiedPriorMerge.note: A GitHub merged-PR search for this author and repository with at least one merge marks the author established, lifting the three-slot limit.

ambiguousCloseKeepsAuthorSlotTest.note: A failed review with a pending close keeps occupying its slot and blocks both restart and other items.

confirmedCloseCountsOnceTest.note: Confirmation replaces ClosePending by CloseConfirmed on the same slot, so the close occupies exactly one slot.

definitiveCloseRefusalReleasesFailedRevi.note: A rejected close plus a failed review leaves the slot unoccupied for the next item.

establishedAuthorMayExceedNewAuthorLimit.note: An established author is not limited, while their slots still occupy.

expiredReviewCanReclaimItsOwnSlotTest.note: An expired running slot is restartable for the same key and occupiedByOthers excludes the key itself.

expiredSentReviewRetainsSlotTest.note: A pending close occupies the slot after lease expiry; elapsed time never frees it.

expiredUnsentReviewReleasesSlotTest.note: An expired claim without a pending close stops occupying, so another item may claim.

failedUnsentReviewReleasesSlotTest.note: A failed slot without a pending close no longer occupies, so another item may start.

newAuthorLastSlotIsAtomicTest.note: The check and claim are one conditional write; with three other slots occupied a new author's review cannot start.

checkpoint.note: The dispatch record is written after the send; the successor does not require a prior send in the guard but stepBlocksImmutable keeps it once set.

nextClaim.note: A newer claim of the review key clears the current block, making the earlier block history that can no longer resume.

remove.note: Installation removal or suspension through the installation machine makes resumable() false.

send.note: A due, undispatched block of the current failed claim with an active installation sends its identifier-only job; repeat sends are allowed until the dispatch record is written.

tick.note: Time advances toward the block's retryAt.

oldClaimCannotResumeTest.note: After a newer claim the old block is no longer current and cannot resume.

queueLostResponseRetriedTest.note: A lost dispatch record lets a later run send again; the duplicate is absorbed by the review claim.

acknowledgeComment.note: After confirmation the close comment is retried until GitHub confirms it, once.

confirm.note: Confirmation by the Slopbot App's close event moves the pending attempt into the close facts in one write, so it is never counted twice.

definitiveRejection.note: A definitive 401/403/404/410/422/429 refusal removes the pending attempt and retains its ID in rejected history.

dispatch.note: The close request is sent at most once for the pending attempt under the reserving lease.

externalClose.note: GitHub applying the close is consumed as CloseEvidence; the close time is carried into the close fact at confirmation rather than stored as a separate step.

loseResponse.note: A lost or ambiguous response leaves the attempt pending; only close evidence or a definitive refusal resolves it.

observe.note: The reservation reads the current registry fence and lease in the same write instead of a separately observed generation; a stale fence returns FenceChanged.

reopen.note: A maintainer reopen is recorded as reversal evidence for the breaker; the reopened close stays in closesInDay, and a new revision of the item is admissible because AlreadyClosed is keyed by item and revision.

replay.note: Replaying a confirmed attempt sends nothing and leaves it confirmed.

reserve.note: One serialized D1 write admits a reservation only below the daily cap counting rolling-day closes plus pending attempts, with breaker, fence, lease and one pending attempt per item.

revoke.note: A changed approved revision, manifest, enforcement position or lease makes admission FenceChanged or LeaseLost.

tick.note: Time advances monotonically; closes age out of the rolling day but pending attempts never do.

tripBreaker.note: The breaker is derived from more than one in ten recent closes being reversed rather than an independent flag.

breakerDoesNotEraseUnknownRequestTest.note: Recording reversals or time never changes pending attempts; a tripped breaker only stops new reservations.

breakerTripsBeforeReservationTest.note: A reservation requires breakerAllows on the same write.

changedAuthorityLosesQueuedReservationTe.note: A changed fence or lease never admits a reservation.

concurrentLastSlotHasOneWinnerTest.note: Serialized reservations count pending attempts, so at the cap only one reservation is admitted.

confirmedHistoryDoesNotDoubleCountTest.note: Confirmation moves the attempt into the close facts and the slot frees once the close leaves the rolling day.

definitiveRefusalReleasesSlotAndKeepsHis.note: A definitive refusal releases the slot, keeps the rejected attempt ID, and a retry reserves a new attempt ID.

lateCompletionReconcilesWithoutResending.note: A late GitHub close confirms the pending attempt and the comment is confirmed without a second request.

reopenedItemMayCloseNewHeadNextDayTest.note: The reopened close still counts for the rolling day; the next day a new revision of the item is admissible since AlreadyClosed is keyed by revision.

timeoutDoesNotFreeSlotTest.note: A pending attempt keeps counting after a day; time alone never frees it.

changeKey.note: The successor never recomputes the attempt's identity: the attempt is bound to its decided candidate, so a changed review digest cannot strand recovery; key recomputation itself is not modelled as a transition.

complete.note: The review completes only under its live claim and only after its close settled; the comment is a separate idempotent confirmCloseComment.

confirm.note: GitHub's close event by the Slopbot App confirms the attempt; confirmation is final and idempotent.

crash.note: A crash is a review finishing Failed (or its lease lapsing); a confirmed attempt stays confirmed and the comment remains retryable.

humanClose.note: A human close event (closedBy HumanActor) cannot confirm the attempt, so it stays pending.

penalize.note: The debit is recorded once per PR node only for a category with a debit; the composition writes it in the same transaction as confirmClose, so no crash window between confirm and penalty exists.

recover.note: A claim made while the close is pending is a Reconcile claim that only reconciles that attempt from GitHub's evidence and never calls a provider or resends; it may start even while the item is open, but cannot complete until confirmed or rejected.

refuse.note: A definitive refusal releases the attempt with its ID retained; no debit is written because only confirmClose writes penalties.

reserve.note: The attempt is bound to its decided candidate identity, fence, lease and reservation sequence; penalty eligibility is derived from the category debit in the points penalty journal rather than stored on the attempt.

retryHumanClosed.note: A human-closed item never yields Slopbot close evidence, so the attempt stays pending.

retryWhileOpen.note: While GitHub shows no close evidence, the unknown attempt stays pending.

send.note: The request is marked once under the reserving lease; a lost response is not a separate transition and leaves the attempt pending.

confirmedCloseFailedBeforeCommentRecover.note: After confirmation the close comment is retried until GitHub confirms it.

definitiveRefusalReleasesWithoutPenaltyT.note: A definitive refusal releases the attempt and no penalty row exists without a confirmed close.

deliveredCloseCannotRecoverAgainTest.note: A completed review keeps its verdict and a confirmed close is no longer pending, so no reconcile claim is due.

humanCloseKeepsSlotPendingTest.note: A human close cannot confirm the attempt, so it stays pending and keeps occupying capacity with no debit.

ineligibleCloseRecordsNoDebitTest.note: A category with no debit records no penalty row.

lostResponseRecoversAfterKeyChangeTest.note: Recovery is bound to the recorded candidate identity, which never changes, so a recomputed key cannot block confirmation.

lostResponseRecoversUnderSameKeyTest.note: A Reconcile claim completes only after the close is confirmed.

openItemKeepsUnknownAttemptPendingTest.note: Without close evidence the attempt stays pending; the successor allows a Reconcile claim that cannot complete, whereas legacy refused recovery outright.

penalizedCloseFailedBeforeFinishRecovers.note: The PR node keys the debit, so a retry never debits twice.

comment.note: The successor's canConfirmCloseComment only requires sender slopbotWorker and a confirmed attempt; add L::ownsClaim(c.lease, token) so a stale worker cannot publish the close comment over the recovering claim's owner.

confirmFact.note: The close fact is confirmed from GitHub's evidence by the webhook sender, independent of any lease.

dispatch.note: Only the reserving live lease sends the close request.

expire.note: Lease expiry is time passing the claim's expiry; ownsClaim then fails.

externalClose.note: GitHub's close is environment evidence consumed by confirmClose.

finish.note: Only the current unexpired claim owner may finish the review.

oldReply.note: A late original response can only confirm the immutable close fact (by GitHub evidence); it cannot finish the successor's review.

recoverClaim.note: An expired claim can be replaced by a newer token; with a pending close the new claim is a Reconcile claim.

stalePublication.note: A worker whose token is not the live owner cannot finish; stepCompleteRetainsVerdict keeps the owner's completion.

knownExternalFactSurvivesLeaseExpiryTest.note: Confirmation needs only GitHub's evidence from the webhook sender, so the close fact is recorded after lease expiry without any comment.

lateOriginalResponseCannotPublishOverRec.note: Completion is fenced by reviewLease ownsClaim, but the close comment publication (confirmCloseComment) is not lease-fenced in the successor; add the live-owner guard so the late original worker cannot publish the comment over the recovery claim.

authority.note: Maintainer authorship (authorRole) and the PR kind are observed in the gate's source observation; closePolicyFor requires NonMaintainer and PullRequest.

closeAccount.note: Account closure records the membership as closed; closure.md participationAuthority then refuses because membership is not MemberActive.

evaluate.note: Closure authority is computed from the active membership, the author's own recorded pull_request_opened event, a non-maintainer author and a PR; routing still admits advisory review for participants (route AdvisoryReview when closureEligible is false).

reopenExplicitly.note: Only an explicit reopen restores an active membership; ordinary sign-in cannot.

closedMembershipTest.note: A closed membership refuses closure; the recorded run remains, and routing's participants audience still allows advisory review.

explicitReopenTest.note: An explicit reopen makes the membership active again, after which participationAuthority can hold.

maintainerExcludedTest.note: closePolicyFor requires authorRole NonMaintainer, so a maintainer author is never closure-eligible.

comparePage.note: The compare range must report the same total, list exactly that many distinct commits and include every listed commit; page-level structure is abstracted into compareTotal/compareDistinct/compareCoversListed, and commit-hash validity is not separately modelled.

finishListing.note: A listing equal to the total is complete; only exactly 250 listed with a larger total may use the compare fallback; any other shortfall refuses the census.

listedCommit.note: Commits are paged without repeats (distinctCommits) and counted as listedCommits.

publish.note: Only a census where every PR's commits are complete is usable; any incomplete PR refuses the whole census.

rangeHeads.note: pullCommitsComplete has no check that the compare range's base and head are present and valid for the PR; add a compare-range head validity field (e.g. compareHeadsValid) required in the 250-limit branch so a missing head cannot complete.

arbitraryShortListingCannotUseFallbackTe.note: A shortfall other than the 250 listing limit refuses the census.

duplicateAcrossPagesCannotCompleteTest.note: Duplicates reduce compareDistinct below the total, so the census refuses.

listingCeilingRecoversThroughCompleteCom.note: A 250-listed PR with a larger total completes through a matching compare range (sample largePull).

missingHeadCannotCompleteTest.note: No successor field or guard requires valid range heads before the compare fallback; add it to pullCommitsComplete.

movingCompareCountCannotCompleteTest.note: compareTotal must equal totalCommits, so a changed compare count refuses.

omittedListedCommitCannotCompleteTest.note: compareCoversListed must hold, so a compare omitting a listed commit refuses.

shortLastPageCannotCompleteTest.note: compareDistinct must equal the total, so a short compare refuses.

acceptEvidence.note: Incomplete evidence (any limitation) yields SourceIncomplete, so no model is called and nothing is scored.

finishPages.note: The listing is complete only when items equal GitHub's reported count with no cap reached.

page.note: Each page is read until a short page; repeated keys make the listing incomplete.

readBlob.note: Blob reads are bounded to 48 reads, 512 KiB each and 2 MiB per reader; reused verified blobs spend no budget.

rejectBlob.note: A mismatched hash never counts; the evidence becomes a named limitation.

verifyBlob.note: A blob counts only when its computed Git object hash equals the reported SHA within budget.

completeEvidenceTest.note: Complete pages plus hash-verified blobs make the evidence usable.

corruptBlobRefusedTest.note: A corrupt blob is not verified, so the evidence is incomplete.

admit.note: An import needs a verified administrator, a deployed producer revision, a labelled subscription producer and every source closed before 1 November 2026.

collect.note: Acceptance binds the exact distinct registered sources into the imported record; collection is not a separate phase.

publish.note: An acceptable request is appended once per assessment key; publication through the work-unit append is a stated composition obligation, and the legacy needs-reconstruction guard is missing (see reconstruct gap).

reconstruct.note: No successor rule models the optional Git merge reconstruction (value-merge-resolution) or requires it to bind the exact input set before publication; add a reconstruction step and a guard that a source needing reconstruction cannot be imported until it is bound.

apiEraWorkRejectedTest.note: Work on or after the API start is refused by the import.

privateHistoricalImportTest.note: A subscription import of pre-start work is recorded once; the reconstruction step of the legacy run has no successor counterpart.

admit.note: Admission needs a current checked owner, no retained result, configured budget, fewer than three occupied slots and a fresh attempt ID.

call.note: Only a reserved (HeldBudget) attempt of a current checked owner may call the next provider on the route.

chooseRecord.note: Nondeterministic scheduler helper of the legacy model; the successor's simulation picks transitions directly.

chooseRequest.note: Nondeterministic scheduler helper of the legacy model; the successor's simulation picks transitions directly.

complete.note: Completion follows saved usage and any required retention; a no-call attempt reaches RouteDone through endWithoutCall or skipUnavailable.

deliver.note: Delayed delivery of the D1 batch response is a shell transport detail; the successor's reserve is one atomic transition whose decision cannot be reclassified by later writes.

exhaustBudget.note: Budget exhaustion is an observation of usage, holds and the cap; admission then returns BudgetBlocked.

lackAtomicStorage.note: The successor's reserve is defined as a single atomic conditional write; a store lacking atomic batches cannot realize that transition, and canCall requires the HeldBudget stage only reserve sets.

loseOwner.note: Ownership lapses when the request deadline passes; canReserve and canCall require checkedCurrent ownership.

reconcileZero.note: Reconciling a completed attempt with no calls removes it from occupied.

record.note: Each call is recorded on the attempt; saving usage frees the slot only when every call was a budget denial (chargeFree).

rejectAdmission.note: With three occupied slots admission returns PendingCapacity, or AttemptsExhausted when three completed non-free attempts exist; the refusal is not stored as a row.

reserve.note: Reservation recomputes admission atomically; only Eligible reserves and occupies a slot; budget and capacity refusals leave the attempt Admitted.

restoreBudget.note: When usage and holds fit the cap again budgetAllows holds.

budgetRefusalRetainsOnlyAdmissionTest.note: BudgetBlocked leaves the attempt Admitted without a reservation or slot.

calledAttemptCannotReconcileAsZeroTest.note: Reconciling an attempt with calls marks it reconciled but never frees its slot; the legacy refused the reconcile itself.

completedNoCallReconciliationReleasesCap.note: Reconciling a completed no-call attempt frees its slot for a new reservation.

completedNoCallReservationStillHoldsCapa.note: Completion alone does not free a no-call slot; only reconcile does.

firstReservationWinsLastSlotTest.note: The second reservation sees three occupied slots and gets PendingCapacity.

immutableAttemptCannotBeReadmittedTest.note: canAdmit requires an unused attempt ID, so an attempt is never readmitted.

knownFullAdmissionIsTerminalTest.note: Three completed non-free attempts without a retained result make admission AttemptsExhausted.

missingAtomicStorageCannotAuthorizeCallT.note: No call is possible without the atomic reserve that sets HeldBudget; the explicit storage refusal code is not modelled.

nonFreeReceiptDoesNotReopenSlotTest.note: A non-free call keeps the slot occupied after usage is saved.

recordedNonFreeBeforeCompletionRemainsPe.note: terminal counts only Completed attempts, so a recorded but uncompleted non-free attempt yields PendingCapacity.

refusalSurvivesFreeReceiptBeforeReplyTes.note: A free receipt frees its slot only when usage is saved, after which a new attempt may reserve; the delayed-reply ordering is abstracted.

reverseReservationOrderWinsLastSlotTest.note: Order does not matter; whichever reserves first takes the last slot.

staleOwnerCannotTakeFourthSlotTest.note: A reservation requires a current checked owner and fewer than three slots.

staleOwnerReservationRemainsHeldTest.note: A reserved attempt whose owner lapsed cannot call and keeps its slot until usage or zero-call reconciliation.

unknownFullAdmissionRemainsPendingTest.note: With three occupied but not three terminal attempts, admission is PendingCapacity.

unknownReservationsDoNotExpireTest.note: No age-based action releases a held slot.

admit.note: Admission requires no retained result and fewer than three occupied slots.

budgetRefused.note: A BudgetBlocked attempt stays Admitted without a reservation and consumes no slot.

call.note: A reserved attempt of the current owner calls the next provider.

complete.note: Completion follows saved usage and retention of a valid result.

finish.note: Legacy one-active-caller harness step clearing the current attempt; the successor keeps requests and attempts as independent lists with no current pointer.

freeDenial.note: A recognized Surplus spending denial is recorded as BudgetDenial; an attempt whose calls are all denials is free once usage is saved.

mixedDenial.note: An attempt with any non-denial call (e.g. Orbio after a denial) is non-free and stays counted.

publish.note: Publication appends the retained result under the current fence, reusing a retained result without another charge.

reconcileZeroCall.note: A completed zero-call attempt is reconciled and released.

recordUsage.note: Usage is saved after the route finishes; saving frees the slot only for an all-denial attempt.

reserve.note: Reservation occupies a slot only when admission is Eligible.

retain.note: Only a saved-usage attempt whose last call is a ValidResult may retain, and only the first retained result wins.

validate.note: A ValidResult needs output from the expected model with a band 0-5, and the proposal must pass the evidence-backed schema check.

calledAttemptCannotReconcileAsZeroTest.note: An attempt with calls is never removed from occupied by reconcile; the successor marks it reconciled where legacy refused.

completedNoCallCannotStartProviderTest.note: canCall requires stage HeldBudget, so a Completed attempt cannot call.

completionAloneKeepsNoCallAttemptCounted.note: complete does not change occupied; reconcile does for zero calls.

freeDenialsLeaveThreeCountedAttemptsTest.note: Free denials release their slots; three non-free attempts fill the limit.

mixedBudgetDenialStillCountsTest.note: chargeFree requires every call to be a denial, so a mixed attempt stays counted.

retainedResultReusedTest.note: A retained result survives and is published without a new attempt; admission returns RetainedResult.

unknownNoCallReservationsRemainCountedTe.note: Reserved attempts without calls stay occupied until completed and reconciled.

unrecordedFreeResponseRemainsCountedTest.note: A denial frees the slot only after its usage is saved.

unreservedAdmissionDoesNotSpendAttemptTe.note: Only reserve adds to occupied, so budget-refused admissions spend no slot.

usageFailureCannotPublishTest.note: Retention requires saved usage and publication requires a retained result.

zeroCallAttemptsDoNotExhaustLimitTest.note: Each reconciled zero-call attempt frees its slot, so further attempts may run and publish.

event.note: Each installation event applies only when newer, or at a tie for removal (unless removed) or suspension (unless removed or suspended); upserts clear removal but keep suspension.

oldEventCannotReviveTest.note: An older upsert after a removal changes nothing.

permissionsUpsertPreservesSuspensionTest.note: A newer upsert keeps an existing suspension, so the installation stays inactive.

tieRemovalWinsTest.note: At an equal source time removal applies and unsuspend does not.

prepare.note: Drafting is the caller constructing the JointRecord with named predecessors; staleness is checked at append by predecessorOk requiring each parent still current, replacing the legacy draft version snapshot.

publish.note: One transaction appends the record once per assessment key, requires every current record sharing a source or claim to be a named predecessor, and retires all predecessors.

cannotSplitCurrentGroupTest.note: A record covering only part of a current group omits a current owner and is refused, so groups never split.

joinAndCorrectAllSourcesTest.note: Single-source groups merge into a joint group and later corrections supersede whole groups.

closeConfirmedByGithub.note: A close candidate's attempt is confirmed only on GitHub's Slopbot close event after every gate passed on a fresh recheck.

deadline.note: The hold is due seven days after the first durable maintainer notice.

debit.note: A confirmed close records the published debit once per PR, never after a confirmed reopen of that revision.

maintainerReopen.note: A verified maintainer reopen marks the attempt reopened, records the reopen and reverses the debit in one write; Slopbot's own reopen is a separate reopenOwnClose.

policy.note: Qualification, consent, membership, exemption and assignment are observed in the gate observation and evaluated by closePolicyFor/closePathFor, never taken from model text.

review.note: The decision records Advisory, Uncertain, LabelFinding or CloseCandidate; an uncertain finding goes to the maintainer hold.

uncertainLabel.note: After the window, without maintainer action or reversal, the uncertain finding is labeled only, never closed.

absentConsentTest.note: Without saved project consent effective closure is false, so no close path exists.

qualifiedClosureTest.note: A qualified confirmed close debits once, and a maintainer reopen reverses the debit.

uncertainNeverClosesTest.note: An uncertain finding is labeled after the window and never closed or debited.

claim.note: The durable claim precedes delivery for both milestone and failure notices, one claim per milestone threshold or failed call.

freshCall.note: recordCall queues exactly one failure notice for each newly inserted failed Orbio or Surplus row and none for a successful row; the successor Provider type has only Orbio and Surplus, so other providers are outside the ledger rather than modelled as non-notifying.

receipt.note: Delivery records Accepted or Ambiguous once and stepReceiptsAreFinal keeps it; an ambiguous outcome is left for operator reconciliation and never resent.

send.note: The notify request and its receipt are merged into one deliver transition that is enabled only while the claimed notice has NoReceipt, so at most one request per claim.

spending.note: A recorded cost row raising the UTC month total to the next $500 threshold is what makes a milestone notice claimable; the successor derives 'earned' from monthTotal instead of a counter.

ambiguousNeverResendsTest.note: Delivery requires NoReceipt, so after an Ambiguous receipt the notice can never be delivered again.

historicalCostsCreateNoBacklogTest.note: The initial ledger holds a failed historical row and the invariant requires zero notices for historical rows, so no backlog is claimable.

primaryAndBackupFailuresBothNotifyTest.note: Each new failed Orbio and Surplus row queues its own notice, each claimed and delivered once.

retainedMilestonesTest.note: Successive $500 milestones are each claimed once and consecutively and their receipts are retained.

successfulAndOtherCallsNeverNotifyTest.note: A NotFailed row queues no notice; the 'other provider' case is absent because the successor ledger's Provider type contains only Orbio and Surplus.

acceptedDrift.note: Accepted bytes differing from the replayed parent make replayEqualsAccepted false, discarding the proof.

ambiguousParent.note: Line-level context matching against repeated parent lines is hand-written byte work under //@ contracts in apps/slopbot (valueEvidence.md intro: 'hunk replay'); the spec sees only the typed per-file result replayEqualsAccepted, which an ambiguous unmatched occurrence makes false.

identicalRepeatedEdits.note: Applying an identical replacement at every repeated occurrence is byte-level hunk replay delegated to the //@-contracted TypeScript in apps/slopbot (valueEvidence.md intro); the spec consumes only replayEqualsAccepted.

partialPatch.note: An incomplete patch fails sameHunks/replayed-count checks so replayComplete is false and the whole proof is discarded.

verify.note: The replay proof counts only when every submitted file replays onto the single accepted parent to exactly the accepted bytes with identical hunks.

allRepeatedEditsVerifiedTest.note: Positive acceptance of identical edits at every repeated occurrence is a property of the byte-level hunk replay under //@ contracts in apps/slopbot, not of the typed ReplayFile results (valueEvidence.md intro).

ambiguousContextRefusedTest.note: An ambiguous context yields a file whose replay does not equal the accepted bytes, which discards the proof; the occurrence counting itself lives in the //@ byte contracts.

exactReplayTest.note: A single-parent, single-file replay whose result equals the accepted bytes is complete.

partialPatchRefusedTest.note: replayComplete requires every submitted path replayed with sameHunks, so a partial patch is refused.

uncoveredDuplicateRefusedTest.note: In the legacy run the replayed bytes happen to equal the drifted accepted bytes, but the uncovered duplicate occurrence means the submitted hunks differ from the accepted ones; the successor refuses this through sameHunks in replayFileHolds, so replayComplete is false (occurrence coverage itself is byte work under //@ contracts).

appeal.note: The author opens one appeal per item revision, binding the revision and open time later used as the reversal authority.

close.note: A confirmed Slopbot close of the current revision is the close-attempt confirmation; it supplies the ConfirmedClose consumed by points/penalties.md recordPenalty.

lateReopenReversal.note: A later close job's reversal uses the reopened revision and its event time as a MaintainerReopen authority, reversing only a covered debit, so a later head's debit survives.

push.note: A new head revision is a GitHub event; the successor represents revisions as strings on ConfirmedClose, Reopen and ReversalAuthority rather than a push transition.

record.note: The debit is written once per PR node and refused when the closed revision already has a confirmed reopen; replays are refused by hasRow instead of being no-ops.

reopen.note: A verified maintainer reopen is recorded and reverses the item's debit only when it covers that revision or a debit recorded at or before the reopen.

tick.note: The three-step clock is replaced by explicit event times (ConfirmedClose.closedAt, Reopen.at, ReversalAuthority.at) in points/penalties.md.

uphold.note: An upheld appeal reverses the debit with reason AppealUpheld only when it covers the appealed revision or a debit recorded at or before the appeal opened.

appealUpholdReversesCoveredDebitTest.note: An upheld appeal covering the debited revision reverses it with AppealUpheld.

lateReopenReversesOwnRevisionDebitTest.note: A reopen of the debited revision reverses its debit with MaintainerReopen.

newerHeadDebitSurvivesOlderAppealTest.note: An older-revision appeal only covers its own revision or debits recorded at or before it opened, so a later head's debit stands.

olderCloseJobKeepsLaterHeadDebitTest.note: The older revision's late reversal authority does not cover the later head's debit recorded after the reopen.

reopenBeforeRecordWritesNoDebitTest.note: reopenedRevision blocks the debit write after a confirmed reopen of the closed revision.

reopenReversesRecordedDebitOnceTest.note: A reopen reverses the recorded debit with MaintainerReopen and a reversed row cannot be reversed again (canReversePenalty needs an unreversed covered row).

secondCloseNeverDebitsAgainTest.note: The PR node keys the debit, so a second close of a later revision records nothing.

spamCloseDebitsOnceAcrossReplaysTest.note: hasRow refuses a replayed record so the item has exactly one debit row.

apiCall.note: A provider call needs the held reservation, a fresh current check and an unfinished route of at most three steps.

apiFailure.note: A FailedCall row advances the route to its successor and ends the route after the third step.

apiSuccess.note: A ValidResult is accepted only with output and a served model equal to the exact expected model of that route step, binding the API producer.

authorityLost.note: Losing ownership or local authority ends the attempt without a call, and every fallback call needs a fresh checkedCurrent check.

historicalMetadata.note: Add a rule that a retained assessment whose API producer route has since been retired stays readable (exactProducer judged against the record's own producer, not the current route) and that reading it creates no call, charge or receipt; today exactProducer is an unconstrained observation flag.

missingOrbio.note: A missing credential skips its route step with no call and no receipt; the route now orders Surplus Sonnet, Surplus Terra, Orbio Sonnet (operator decision of 16 November 2026), so the skipped step need not be Orbio.

retain.note: Only a saved-usage ValidResult with the exact model is retained as the attempt's result.

spendingDenied.note: A Surplus BudgetDenial is recorded; unlike the legacy model it no longer stops the route but skips the remaining Surplus step and asks Orbio (operator decision of 16 November 2026).

subscription.note: A subscription producer is a distinct Producer constructor accepted only by the historical import and never carries billing proof.

allThreeFailuresExhaustRouteTest.note: A FailedCall at routeStep 2 finishes the route and canCall needs routeStep < 3, so three failures end the attempt without a retained result.

budgetDenialStopsRouteTest.note: Superseded by the operator decision of 16 November 2026 recorded in valueInference.md: a Surplus spending denial now skips the remaining Surplus step and asks Orbio in the same attempt (recordCall, sometimesOrbioAfterADenial); the route stops only when Orbio has no key or no valid result.

fallbackHasIndependentAdmissionTest.note: call resets the request check to NoCheck, so a fallback call needs a new current check and lost authority ends the attempt without calling.

missingOrbioDoesNotCreateReceiptTest.note: A missing-credential step is skipped with no Charge appended, and the next step may still call and retain; route order is now Surplus first.

orbioFailureImmediatelyReachesSurplusBac.note: A FailedCall advances to the next provider and a later ValidResult is retained; the order is now Surplus Sonnet, Surplus Terra, then Orbio Sonnet.

retiredProducerHistoryStillReadsTest.note: No successor rule states that a record from a retired API route remains readable and reusable without minting a receipt or authorizing a new call; add a law over decision/exactProducer for retired producers.

subscriptionNeverClaimsApiReceiptTest.note: A subscription declaration never has billingProof.

record.note: Each call appends an immutable new row billed zero while the historical row keeps its original billed amount; the successor ledger stores one chosen amount, and the known/actual versus estimate split is kept on valueInference Charge rows.

noInferredHistoricalReceiptTest.note: The legacy test keeps an unknown actual cost (-1) distinct from the local estimate and from a reported zero on every append-only row, including the historical call-v1 row; the successor CostRow stores only one chosen amount with no known/unknown actual flag, so add an actualKnown (or providerReported) field to CostRow plus a law that an unreported or historical row is never read as a known actual receipt and a step law that existing cost rows are never rewritten.

captureA.note: The publisher captures registry revision, manifest and enforcement generation before collection.

captureB.note: A second owner captures its own fence; only the current group owner may do so.

commitA.note: Publication needs the retained result, a current check and a fence equal to the current authority, and is refused once something is published.

commitB.note: A competing publisher cannot write a second publication; the existing one is retained. The legacy replay-return of the existing record is a value request Current outcome rather than a second write.

pause.note: A paused project advances the observed authority revision, so the captured fence no longer matches and publication refuses.

quarantine.note: A restriction advances the enforcement generation, invalidating the captured fence.

removeSecondary.note: A membership read that no longer covers the exact group sets remoteExact false, so the request is not current and cannot publish.

competingPublisherIsReplayTest.note: Exactly one publication of the retained result is written; the second publisher is refused rather than writing, and reads the existing record as current through value history.

lateReplayDoesNotWriteTest.note: After publication and a pause, a late publisher cannot write and the existing publication is unchanged.

pauseBeforeInsertWinsTest.note: A fence captured before the pause differs from the current authority, so publication refuses.

removedGroupMemberWinsTest.note: A removed group member makes the membership inexact and refuses publication.

restrictionBeforeInsertWinsTest.note: A generation change after capture refuses publication.

accept.note: A receipt counts only when every check holds and it is unexpired; closure eligibility additionally needs objectiveCloseQualified with the qualified profile and a shadow record.

inspect.note: Subject binding, approved-vm isolation, zero visibility gaps, guidance rule and kind predicate are independent conjuncts of receiptCounts.

qualify.note: Profile qualification is a separate decided-qualifier transition, kept unset at launch.

tick.note: The clock is the now parameter of receiptCounts; expiry is the law lawExpiredReceiptNeverCounts in closureActivation.md.

verify.note: A valid signature by the configured verifier key is one necessary conjunct of receiptCounts.

expiredReceiptRefusedTest.note: A receipt with expiresAt at or before now never counts.

receiptDoesNotQualifyProfileTest.note: A counted receipt with no qualified verifier profile never qualifies objective closure.

signatureDoesNotProveCoverageTest.note: A valid signature without zero visibility gaps and a holding predicate does not count.

identity.note: The repository ID and the permission's GitHub account ID must match the query.

installation.note: Missing and suspended installations answer without a token; only an installed lookup proceeds.

issue.note: An installed answer requires an issued token.

permission.note: The answered permission is the observed collaborator permission, none for a non-collaborator.

unavailable.note: Any failed or mismatched read falls through to 503 unavailable, granting nothing.

livePermissionTest.note: Matching installation, repository and account facts answer the observed write permission.

reusedLoginIsNotAuthorityTest.note: A login now held by another account ID never yields an Installed answer.

begin.note: A malformed query answers 400 before any lookup and each request is answered independently; the legacy unsafe-numeric-ID class (503 without a token) is not carried and is recorded as the unsafeNumericIdRequestsNoTokenTest gap.

facts.note: The repository read must report the expected repository ID; the optional full repository facts validation is not modelled (see requestedFullFactsRemainValidatedTest gap).

identified.note: Composite test helper (start, issue, facts) with no behaviour of its own.

installation.note: Missing and suspended installations answer 200 with that kind, a failed lookup answers 503.

issue.note: An installed answer requires tokenIssued; a failed issue answers 503.

legacyToken.note: The installation-wide token and the handleRepositoryRead relay are retired (model header); kept in legacy only as a negative control.

movePath.note: A repository path that now resolves to another ID is observed as repositoryIdSeen differing from the query, which never answers Installed.

permission.note: A missing collaborator is none, a failed or unknown permission read is unavailable, and the permission must belong to the expected account ID.

permissionChanges.note: Permission changes are GitHub environment events; the successor answer is a pure function of the facts read for the request and does not claim continuous ownership.

respond.note: The answer is no-store, carries no token, and reports the observed permission.

reuseLogin.note: A login reused by another account fails the account ID binding.

start.note: Composite test helper (begin then installation) with no behaviour of its own.

failedPermissionReadDoesNotClaimNoneTest.note: permissionLookupFailed answers 503 unavailable rather than none.

invalidInstallationIsUnavailableTest.note: A failed or invalid installation lookup answers 503 unavailable.

invalidPermissionLevelIsUnavailableTest.note: An unknown permission level is never answered as Installed.

laterRevocationDoesNotRewriteObservedPer.note: The answer is a pure function of the facts read for that request, so a later change does not rewrite it.

malformedRouteRequestsNoTokenTest.note: A malformed repository or login answers 400 invalid_request.

matchingRepositoryRetainsPermissionTest.note: Matching facts answer Installed with the observed permission.

mismatchedRepositoryIdStillRefusesTest.note: A repository ID mismatch never answers Installed.

missingInstallationReturnsMissingTest.note: LookupMissing answers NotInstalled without a token.

oldInstallationWideTokenLendsReplacement.note: Negative control for the retired installation-wide token relay; the scoped-token rule it motivates is recorded as the tokenHasOnlyExpectedRepositoryAndMetadataTest gap.

omittedFullFactsStillChecksRepositoryIdT.note: The repository ID check applies regardless of whether full facts are requested.

pathReuseBeforeFactsCannotPassIdentityTe.note: A path moved before the repository read reports another repository ID and never answers Installed.

pathReuseBetweenReadsCannotLendPermissio.note: The successor collapses the repository and permission reads into one AccessFacts, so a path moving between the two reads is not representable; add a separate permission-read repository fact and a law that, with a token scoped to the expected repository, a moved path's permission read yields none rather than lending the other repository's permission.

requestedFullFactsRemainValidatedTest.note: includeRepository=1 is prose only; add an includeRepository query flag and a fullFactsValid fact with a law that a requested but invalid full repository identity answers 503.

restoredPathAllowsIndependentRetryTest.note: Each request is answered independently from its own facts, so a retry after the path is restored answers write.

reusedLoginStillFailsActorIdentityTest.note: A collaborator answer for another account ID is refused.

suspendedInstallationRequestsNoTokenTest.note: LookupSuspended answers InstallationSuspended before any token; the no-token-requested order is prose.

tokenHasOnlyExpectedRepositoryAndMetadat.note: The prose says the token is metadata-read and scoped to exactly the expected repository ID, but AccessFacts only has tokenIssued; add token scope fields (repositoryIds, metadataOnly) and a law that an Installed answer requires a token scoped to exactly the queried repository with metadata read only.

unsafeNumericIdRequestsNoTokenTest.note: accessQueryValid only requires repositoryId > 0; add a safe-integer bound on repositoryId and githubId so an ID beyond the safe range is refused before any token request (legacy answers 503 unavailable).

classifyPromotion.note: A covered identical-tree promotion is recorded once and adds no unit or value.

hint.note: Commit hints only discover candidates; merge reconstruction, ancestry and retained copies are verified shell evidence of the merge verifier, consumed only as results (slopbot/workUnits.md 'A claim is one changed path...', points/workUnits.md hashesVerified adapter obligation).

observeRegisteredBranch.note: Reading the registered integration branch is GitHub shell evidence feeding GroupEvidence.hashesVerified (points/workUnits.md adapter obligation).

original.note: Every imported commit must belong to an earlier accepted current unit of the same project; the legacy 'exactly one original' is relaxed to 'some accepted unit'.

verifyAncestry.note: Ancestry verification is merge-verifier shell evidence consumed as a result (slopbot/workUnits.md).

verifyRetainedTrees.note: Complete hash-verified trees are the Promotion evidence; missing trees hold the promotion unresolved.

hintIsNotAcceptanceTest.note: Both forming a unit and recording a promotion require hashesVerified evidence, so an unverified hint alone accepts nothing.

unchangedPromotionHasNoAdditionalCreditT.note: A verified no-change promotion covered by accepted originals is recorded without a new unit or credit.

context.note: Nondeterministic item context is the RouteInput argument of route in slopbot/routing.md.

route.note: The first failing condition decides; advisory review stays broad while MayCloseReview needs a closure-eligible non-exempt pull request in contributor scope.

humanReopenPreservedTest.note: A human reopen of this revision stops review and therefore closure.

pausedSecurityOnlyTest.note: Security-only scope routes to SecurityReviewOnly, which reviews but never closes.

call.note: Only the current unexpired owner records a provider call.

finish.note: Only the current unexpired token records failed, skipped or completed.

obsolete.note: A stale or expired token does not own the claim and so cannot finish or call.

start.note: A higher token claims an absent, skipped, failed or expired review and the kind records first, retry or reconcile.

tick.note: Time advances monotonically.

expiredWorkerCannotFinishTest.note: An expired claim grants no finish even before takeover.

failedCallIsRetryTest.note: A claim after a failed status or a recorded call is a Retry.

skippedBeforeInferenceIsNewTest.note: A skipped review with no recorded call restarts as a First attempt.

takeoverFencesOldWorkerTest.note: A takeover after expiry raises the token, the old token is fenced, and the new owner completes as a retry.

claimA.note: The whole group is leased in one write, refused if any source belongs to another live claim's group.

claimB.note: The same all-or-nothing group lease applies to the second claim.

publishA.note: Publication rechecks the live claim and its exact group.

publishB.note: Publication rechecks the live claim and its exact group.

startA.note: A delivery takes a ten-minute running claim before leasing sources.

startB.note: A second delivery takes its own running claim.

tick.note: Time advances; an expired claim no longer blocks.

expiredGroupCanBeReclaimedTest.note: Groups of expired claims do not block and are dropped when a new group is claimed.

overlapBlocksSecondOwnerTest.note: An overlapping wanted source refuses the whole second group.

separateSourcesMayProceedTest.note: Disjoint groups are leased and published independently.

admitB.note: Admission returns Eligible under three counted attempts, AttemptsExhausted when three completed non-free attempts exist, and PendingCapacity otherwise.

callB.note: A call needs the held reservation and a current check.

claimB.note: A successor request claims the key with a new token, and it can own the group only when no other request still owns it, i.e. after the previous owner's lease expired (canOwnGroup).

completeA.note: Completion requires saved usage and, for a valid result, prior retention.

dueB.note: A waiting request becomes due after its retry time and may be claimed again.

expireA.note: Advancing time past the request deadline ends ownership; the attempt keeps its occupied slot.

firstReadB.note: The admission decision checks a retained result first.

publishA.note: Publication requires a current owner check, so an expired owner cannot publish.

publishB.note: The current owner publishes the retained result under its fence without a new call.

recordA.note: The provider receipt is appended to the attempt and saved usage releases the slot only for a wholly free denial.

replyB.note: The recorded admission becomes a fixed outcome: pending capacity waits, exhausted is terminal, eligible proceeds to reserve.

reserveB.note: A reservation needs an Eligible admission and occupies a slot.

retainA.note: A saved-usage valid result is retained even after the owner's lease expired.

terminalReadB.note: admission places RetainedResult before AttemptsExhausted, so a retained result always wins over terminal classification; the successor evaluates both in one read instead of a second terminal read.

completedNonFreeExhaustionRemainsTermina.note: Three completed non-free attempts without a retained result yield AttemptsExhausted and no call.

completionRequiresSuccessfulRetentionTes.note: A valid result cannot complete before it is retained.

incompleteNonFreeCostDoesNotEndRequestTe.note: An incomplete attempt occupies a slot but is not terminal, so the request waits as PendingCapacity and later reuses the retained result.

lateFreeReceiptResumesAtRetryTest.note: A late wholly free receipt releases its slot on saveUsage, so the next due claim is admitted and may call.

oldOwnerCannotPublishRetainedResultTest.note: The expired owner may retain but cannot publish; a later owner reuses the retained result.

pendingReceiptDoesNotChangeBeforeReplyTe.note: The outcome is fixed from the Observation recorded for the claim, so a receipt arriving after admission changes only the next claim.

retainedBetweenReadAndAdmissionIsRecheck.note: Admission re-evaluates retained first, so a result retained after an earlier read is published instead of exhausting.

unknownHoldsNeverAuthorizeFourthCallTest.note: An interrupted or unreconciled attempt keeps its slot so at most three are counted and no fourth call is admitted.

abandonUncertain.note: Successor has no explicit abandon transition: the attempt is ended by complete, and an unknown or over-maximum charge never satisfies canReconcile, so its reservation stays counted in heldCap/unboundedHold indefinitely, matching the legacy uncertainHeld accounting.

completeNoCall.note: A refusal before the first call ends the attempt with zero calls (endWithoutCall) and complete records explicit completion.

provider.note: A provider charge (known actual or unknown estimate) is appended by recordCall and counted in localUsedAt via chargeTotal with the estimate for unknown costs.

reconcile.note: Reconciliation needs a Completed attempt with all-known charges within the reserved maximum; zero-call reconciliation frees the occupied slot (migration 0118 behaviour).

reserve.note: Reserving an attempt's hold under alerts-only or capped mode is canReserve/reserve gated by budgetAllows (cap includes used, held and the route maximum); successor holds the operator route maximum rather than a per-call amount.

alertsRefusalBeforeCallRestoresCappedMod.note: Reconciling the zero-call alerts attempt clears the unbounded hold, so capped admission is possible again.

authorityRefusalBeforeCallReleasesHoldTe.note: Authority loss before the first call ends without a call; completion and zero-call reconciliation release the hold and the occupied slot.

completedNoCallReleasesCapacityTest.note: A completed zero-call attempt reconciles at zero cost and frees capacity.

exactReconciliationReleasesCapacityTest.note: Reconciling an all-known charge within the maximum removes it from heldCap so later capacity returns.

providerOverchargeRemainsHeldTest.note: canReconcile requires chargeTotal <= maximum for limited attempts, so an overcharge keeps its hold in heldCap.

unfinishedNoCallRemainsHeldTest.note: canReconcile requires stage Completed, so an unfinished no-call attempt cannot release its hold.

unknownAlertsBlockCappedModeTest.note: An unreconciled alerts-only (unlimited) attempt is an unboundedHold, which makes budgetAllows refuse capped admission.

unknownCappedCallRetainsEstimateAndHoldT.note: Unknown cost counts its estimate in localUsedAt and keeps the reservation in heldCap, so a further capped reservation exceeding the cap is refused.
